paras.en: Berman said on Sunday NFL Countdown that Jackson’s death was unexpected and that he had spoken with his best friend “at length” on Tuesday. “He was a vital 75,” he said. On Nov. 1, they spent time on the ESPN set after Jackson arrived for a surprise visit.
paras.zh: 伯曼在周日的 NFL 倒计时节目中表示，杰克逊的去世是出乎意料的，他在周二与他最好的朋友进行了“详细”交谈。 “他是一个充满活力的 75 岁，”他说。 11 月 1 日，杰克逊突然来访后，他们在 ESPN 片场度过了一段时光。

paras.en: “Tom was so much more than an accomplished NFL analyst,” Berman said in his statement. “There was nobody kinder, more thoughtful, more loyal or more engaging than him. And when it came to laughter, Tom’s was frequent and unmistakable. He is easily summed up by this classic old song: ‘He’s got sunshine on a cloudy day.’”
paras.zh: “汤姆不仅仅是一位出色的 NFL 分析师，”伯曼在声明中说道。 “没有人比他更友善、更体贴、更忠诚或更有吸引力。说到笑声，汤姆的笑声频繁且明显。这首经典老歌很容易概括他：‘阴天里有阳光。’”

paras.en: Added ESPN chairman Jimmy Pitaro, “He brought the credibility of an All-Pro NFL player, the insight of a gifted analyst and a warmth and authenticity that connected with generations of football fans.”
paras.zh: ESPN 主席吉米·皮塔罗 (Jimmy Pitaro) 补充道：“他带来了 NFL 全职业球员的可信度、天才分析师的洞察力以及与几代球迷联系在一起的温暖和真实。”

paras.en: ESPN’s NFL studio is named the Chris Berman-Tom Jackson Studio.
paras.zh: ESPN 的 NFL 工作室被命名为克里斯·伯曼-汤姆·杰克逊工作室。

paras.en: Born in Cleveland on April 4, 1951, Thomas Louie Jackson attended John Adams High School in the city before he was recruited by University of Louisville head coach Lee Corso — another future ESPN commentator — to join the Cardinals.
paras.zh: 托马斯·路易·杰克逊 (Thomas Louie Jackson) 1951 年 4 月 4 日出生于克利夫兰，就读于该市的约翰·亚当斯高中 (John Adams High School)，之后被路易斯维尔大学主教练李·科索 (Lee Corso)（另一位未来的 ESPN 评论员）招募加入红雀队。

paras.en: A fourth-round pick (88th overall) by the Broncos in the 1973 NFL Draft, he played in 191 regular-season games, the most in team history when he retired in 1986, and 10 playoff games, all with Denver.
paras.zh: 他在 1973 年 NFL 选秀中被野马队第四轮选秀（总第 88 顺位），参加了 191 场常规赛，这是他 1986 年退役时队史最多的比赛，并在丹佛队参加了 10 场季后赛。

paras.en: He was a first-team All-Pro in 1977 and 1978 and a three-time Pro Bowl selection and inducted into the team’s Ring of Fame in 1992.
paras.zh: 他于 1977 年和 1978 年入选一线队，并三度入选职业碗，并于 1992 年入选球队名人堂。

paras.en: When he retired at 36, Jackson was the NFL’s oldest linebacker.
paras.zh: 杰克逊 36 岁退役时，是 NFL 年龄最大的线卫。

paras.en: “An inspirational leader and fierce competitor, TJ was a proud member of the Broncos’ first Super Bowl team [in 1977] that helped establish a winning tradition in Denver,” the team said in a statement. “Off the field, Tom carried himself with class, warmth and humility, forging deep connections and lifelong friendships with teammates and throughout Broncos Country.”
paras.zh: “TJ 是一位鼓舞人心的领导者和激烈的竞争者，他是野马队 (1977 年) 首支超级碗球队的骄傲成员，帮助丹佛建立了获胜传统，”球队在一份声明中表示。 “在场外，汤姆表现得优雅、热情和谦逊，与队友和整个野马队建立了深厚的联系和终生的友谊。”

paras.en: Jackson’s broadcast career began as a co-host of a Broncos Beat weekly program on KCNC-TV in Denver and postgame show on KUSA-TV. He also hosted a daily Behind the Line syndicated sports commentary radio show and was hired by ESPN in 1987.
paras.zh: 杰克逊的广播生涯始于丹佛 KCNC-TV 野马节拍每周节目和 KUSA-TV 赛后节目的共同主持人。他还主持了每日的 Behind the Line 联合体育评论广播节目，并于 1987 年被 ESPN 聘用。

paras.en: He received a Sports Emmy in 2009 and awarded the prestigious Pete Rozelle Radio-Television Award by the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 2015. He retired from broadcasting a year later but reunited with Berman for a digital-only edition of NFL Primetime in 2019.
paras.zh: 他于 2009 年获得体育艾美奖，并于 2015 年被职业橄榄球名人堂授予著名的皮特·罗泽尔广播电视奖。一年后，他从广播界退休，但在 2019 年与伯曼重聚，制作了纯数字版 NFL 黄金时段。

paras.en: Jackson often said that he had been “blessed to work for two companies in my life: the Denver Broncos and ESPN.”
paras.zh: 杰克逊经常说，他“很幸运能够为我一生中的两家公司工作：丹佛野马队和 ESPN”。

paras.en: Survivors include his wife, Jennifer, and his daughters, Taylor and Morgan. Another daughter, Andrea, died in 1997 at age 9 of injuries suffered in a car accident.
paras.zh: 幸存者包括他的妻子詹妮弗以及他的女儿泰勒和摩根。另一个女儿安德里亚 (Andrea) 于 1997 年因车祸受伤去世，享年 9 岁。

articles.title: After 114 Years, the Beverly Hills Hotel Gets a (Night)life
articles.author: Lexy Perez

paras.en: Wearing a hard hat and a tailored suit, Beverly Hills Hotel general manager John Scanlon surveys the most significant expansion in the iconic Pink Palace’s 114-year history. Amid the BRRRAAAP! of drills and SKREEEE! of scraping metal, he outlines a slate of new amenities, a decade in the making, including a supper club, a screening room and a cocktail bar.
paras.zh: 比佛利山庄酒店 (Beverly Hills Hotel) 总经理约翰·斯坎伦 (John Scanlon) 头戴安全帽，身着定制西装，审视标志性粉红宫 114 年历史中最重大的扩建工程。在轰鸣声中！钻头和SKREEEE！他用刮金属的方法，概述了一系列经过十年打造的新设施，包括晚餐俱乐部、放映室和鸡尾酒吧。

paras.en: “I’m going to bed at night dreaming about this and waking up thinking about it,” says Scanlon, a Dorchester Collection veteran who previously ran London’s 45 Park Lane. “It’s the first thought that comes into my head in the morning: ‘Where are we at? What have we got to do today?’ ”
paras.zh: “我晚上睡觉时会梦见这个，醒来时也会想起它，”斯坎伦说，他是多切斯特收藏集团的资深人士，曾经营伦敦公园巷 45 号。 “早上我脑子里出现的第一个想法是：‘我们现在在哪里？今天我们要做什么？’”

paras.en: Right now, in the lead-up to their simultaneous debut in the coming weeks, the answer is: a lot. Finalize the menus. Hire more staff. Approve the live acts. Close out permits. Eyeball every aesthetic detail. On a terrace, among the property’s paddle-shaped banana leaf plants, Scanlon says in his Irish brogue, with traces of exhilaration and exhaustion, “I’m obsessed.”
paras.zh: 现在，在未来几周他们同时首次亮相之前，答案是：很多。完成菜单。雇用更多员工。批准现场行为。关闭许可证。关注每一个美学细节。在露台上，在酒店桨状的香蕉叶植物丛中，斯坎伦用他的爱尔兰方言说道，语气中带着兴奋和疲惫的痕迹，“我着迷了。”

paras.en: Later, over a lunch of McCarthy salads at the Polo Lounge, alongside the hotel’s new food-and-beverage head Megan Doherty, Scanlon explains that this is all an attempt to better serve guests, especially locals. A consultant — in his accounting, a “social anthropologist” — asked regulars what they wanted as the hotel considered renovations to a sizable swath of neglected, interconnected square footage, on the lobby level to the left of the red carpeted entrance, ranging from an unpopular bedroom suite to a ’90s-era business center that “nobody was using anymore.”
paras.zh: 随后，斯坎伦在 Polo Lounge 与酒店新任餐饮主管梅根·多尔蒂 (Megan Doherty) 一起享用麦卡锡沙拉午餐时解释说，这一切都是为了更好地服务客人，尤其是当地人。一位顾问——在他的会计中，一位“社会人类学家”——询问常客他们想要什么，因为酒店正在考虑对红地毯入口左侧的大堂层一大片被忽视的、相互连接的面积进行翻修，从不受欢迎的卧室套房到“没人再使用”的 90 年代时代的商务中心。

paras.en: Foremost, it turned out, was a desire for a real nightlife option for party-hardly Beverly Hills. The solution is The Supper Club: a 94-seat, high-glam ovular room with skyline views of Century City that aims for neo-retro, akin to Delilah in West Hollywood. Open until 1 a.m., it will feature a no-photos policy, throwback palm tree motifs, coastal Italian dishes from chef Mattia Agazzi (previously of Gucci Osteria) and a sequence of live evening performances, including five-piece bands, which are curated by music director Alex Le Roux, an in-demand industry booker for events like the wedding of Brooklyn Beckham and Nicola Peltz. “This concept perfectly fits into the heritage of this hotel, but allows us to do something fresh,” says Doherty, who previously ran operations for star L.A. chef Evan Funke.
paras.zh: 事实证明，最重要的是希望在几乎没有派对的比佛利山庄拥有真正的夜生活选择。解决方案是 The Supper Club：一间拥有 94 个座位的华丽椭圆形房间，可欣赏世纪城的天际线景观，旨在呈现新复古风格，类似于西好莱坞的黛利拉 (Delilah)。营业至凌晨 1 点，这里将实行禁止拍照政策，采用复古棕榈树图案，主厨 Mattia Agazzi（前 Gucci Osteria）主理的沿海意大利菜肴，以及一系列现场晚间表演，包括由音乐总监 Alex Le Roux 策划的五人乐队表演，他是布鲁克林·贝克汉姆 (Brooklyn Beckham) 和尼古拉·佩尔茨 (Nicola Peltz) 婚礼等热门活动的行业预订者。 “这个概念完全符合这家酒店的传统，但让我们能够做一些新鲜的事情，”曾为洛杉矶明星厨师 Evan Funke 负责运营的 Doherty 说道。

paras.en: The research also produced a 14-seat screening room, which is tricked out for sound to handle record-release listening events. Its design by Ken Fulk (clients include Pharrell Williams and Gigi Hadid) is inspired by the Holmby Hills screening room of , Louis B. Mayer’s daughter and Hollywood’s preeminent hostess, where she showed films to friends before release.
paras.zh: 该研究还建造了一个 14 座的放映室，该放映室经过音响设计，可以处理唱片发行的聆听活动。它的设计由 Ken Fulk（客户包括 Pharrell Williams 和 Gigi Hadid）设计，灵感来自于 Louis B. Mayer 的女儿、好莱坞杰出女主人的 Holmby Hills 放映室，她在电影上映前曾在那里向朋友放映电影。

paras.en: For his part, Scanlon seems perhaps most enthused about a new, yet-unnamed cocktail bar — “very intimate, very elegant” — which he promises will rival the Dorchester’s offerings, as well as a lobby-oriented lounge, boasting a wraparound veranda, which will present afternoon tea service: “We’ll have bespoke teas and hand-painted china from Royal Crown Derby and custom sterling silver tea stands that have been made by Arthur Price. It’s a Claridge’s-level experience.”
paras.zh: 就斯坎伦而言，他似乎最热衷于一个新的、尚未命名的鸡尾酒吧——“非常亲密、非常优雅”——他承诺这将与多切斯特酒店的产品相媲美，还有一个面向大堂的休息室，拥有一个环绕式阳台，将提供下午茶服务：“我们将有来自皇家皇冠德比的定制茶和手绘瓷器，以及由亚瑟·普莱斯制作的定制纯银茶架。克拉里奇级别的体验。”

paras.en: A key challenge for the new spaces is competing with the landmark existing ones, chiefly the Polo Lounge, the Fountain Coffee Room and the Cabana Café. “Our guests know and love and really connect with them, and there’s this nostalgia there,” Scanlon explains. “They are tractor beams. So, with what we’re doing now, it’s been about, ‘What can we do that’s distinctive?’ They need to shine on their own.” He adds, looking up from his McCarthy salad, “a lot of places take the most popular dish off the menu. That’s crazy to me. Make another popular dish!”
paras.zh: 新空间的一个关键挑战是与现有的地标空间竞争，主要是 Polo Lounge、Fountain Coffee Room 和 Cabana Café。 “我们的客人认识他们、喜爱他们，并与他们建立了真正的联系，并且有一种怀旧之情，”斯坎伦解释道。 “它们是牵引光束。所以，我们现在所做的就是‘我们能做些什么独特的事情？’它们需要自己发光。”他从麦卡锡沙拉上抬起头补充道，“很多地方都把最受欢迎的菜从菜单上去掉了。这对我来说太疯狂了。再做一道受欢迎的菜！”

articles.title: The Hotel Bel-Air’s Menu Returns to Tradition
articles.author: Lexy Perez

paras.en: Since Wolfgang Puck’s 2023 departure from the Hotel Bel-Air and its eponymous restaurant, the luxury lodging has been tweaking its Cal-Med menus with classical French techniques and hyper-seasonal ingredients. The approach was ambitious, evolving, at times even experimental. Yet the largely local dining clientele — 70 percent of weekly regulars are neighbors — who treat the place as a second home (or maybe a fourth, given their net worth) have made it clear they prefer familiarity over ingenuity. Under new executive chef Ralf Schlegel (far left), previously of The Peninsula in Beverly Hills, the kitchen has turned back toward the classics.
paras.zh: 自 Wolfgang Puck 于 2023 年离开贝莱尔酒店及其同名餐厅以来，这家豪华酒店一直在用经典的法国技术和超时令食材调整其 Cal-Med 菜单。这种方法雄心勃勃，不断发展，有时甚至是实验性的。然而，大部分就餐顾客都是本地人——70%的每周常客都是邻居——他们把这个地方当作第二个家（或者考虑到他们的净资产，也许是第四个家），他们已经明确表示，他们更喜欢熟悉而不是独创性。曾在比佛利山半岛酒店任职的新任行政总厨拉尔夫·施莱格尔（最左）在他的领导下，厨房又回归了经典。

paras.en: The bill of fare has long had a dedicated section of “Bel-Air Classics”: the tortilla soup, the club sandwich, the chopped salad named for late No. 1 fan Nancy Reagan. Now, the restaurant has restored several other salads that had been relegated to off-menu, only-by-request status — Thai-style chicken, soy ginger BBQ salmon, burrata with squash — along with the house burger.
paras.zh: 菜单上长期以来一直有专门的“贝莱尔经典”部分：玉米饼汤、俱乐部三明治、以已故第一号粉丝南希·里根命名的切碎沙拉。现在，这家餐厅已经恢复了其他几种沙拉，这些沙拉已经被降级为菜单外、只能根据要求提供的状态——泰式鸡肉、大豆生姜烧烤三文鱼、布拉塔配南瓜——以及自家汉堡。

paras.en: “When you go home, you want what you remember,” explains Hotel Bel-Air manager Tiffany Lai, who insists the restaurant’s back-to-basics pivot won’t condemn it to culinary ossification. “We’re still busy creating new favorites.” She points to the German-born, Austria-raised Schlegel’s signature dish: chicken schnitzel with lemon paprika (left). “Maybe in 15 years that’ll be the next classic.”
paras.zh: 贝莱尔酒店经理蒂芙尼·赖 (Tiffany Lai) 解释说：“当你回家时，你会想要你记得的东西。”她坚称餐厅回归本源的理念不会使其烹饪变得僵化。 “我们仍在忙于创造新的最爱。”她指着德国出生、奥地利长大的施莱格尔的招牌菜：柠檬辣椒鸡排（左）。 “也许 15 年后这将成为下一个经典。”

articles.title: Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton warns Americans of 'bumps in the road' after tech outages

paras.en: Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton warned Americans to prepare for "bumps in the road" after a set of damaging technology outages rocked air travel and systems like Microsoft Outlook.
paras.zh: 在一系列破坏性技术中断震撼了航空旅行和 Microsoft Outlook 等系统后，国家情报总监杰伊·克莱顿 (Jay Clayton) 警告美国人要为“道路上的颠簸”做好准备。

paras.en: Government officials have largely dismissed the prospects that the outages, which also slowed bank transactions, are linked to a coordinated or artificial intelligence cyberattack.
paras.zh: 政府官员在很大程度上否认了这种中断与协调或人工智能网络攻击有关的可能性，这种中断也减缓了银行交易。

paras.en: Clayton, however, said on CNN's "State of the Union" that outages may continue as companies and the government upgrade their systems to adapt to the AI age.
paras.zh: 然而，克莱顿在美国有线电视新闻网的“国情咨文”中表示，随着公司和政府升级系统以适应人工智能时代，中断可能会继续。

paras.en: "The American people should be prepared for a great deal of investment in upgrading our systems; they should be prepared for investment in cybersecurity, and they should be prepared that any time there is a step change in technology, a step change in both compute and applications, there will be bumps in the road," Clayton said.
paras.zh: 克莱顿说：“美国人民应该做好准备，为升级我们的系统进行大量投资；他们应该为网络安全投资做好准备，他们应该做好准备，只要技术发生阶跃变化，计算和应用程序发生阶跃变化，道路上就会出现坎坷。”

paras.en: "You prepare by knowing that systems are going to be upgraded; they may be interrupted for a period of time and that companies and government are dealing with this on the front foot," he said.
paras.zh: 他说：“你要做好准备，知道系统将要升级；它们可能会中断一段时间，而公司和政府正在积极应对这一问题。”

paras.en: Clayton's warning came as the U.S. prepares to celebrate Thanksgiving on Thursday, one of the busiest travel weeks of the year. A technology outage prompted a nationwide ground stop just over a week ago, which lasted for hours.
paras.zh: 克莱顿发出警告之际，美国正准备周四庆祝感恩节，感恩节是一年中最繁忙的旅行周之一。一周多前，一次技术故障导致全国范围内停飞，持续了几个小时。

paras.en: The Federal Aviation Administration said router upgrades caused a flood of data that led to the ground stop, and that there is no indication of a cyberattack.
paras.zh: 美国联邦航空管理局表示，路由器升级导致大量数据导致飞机停飞，并且没有迹象表明受到网络攻击。

paras.en: Separately, Microsoft said the Outlook outage was caused by "an issue during an earlier network capacity upgrade."
paras.zh: 另外，微软表示 Outlook 中断是由“早期网络容量升级过程中的问题”引起的。

paras.en: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent delivered a similar message on CBS' "Face the Nation."
paras.zh: 财政部长斯科特·贝森特在哥伦比亚广播公司的“面对国家”节目中也表达了类似的信息。

paras.en: Asked if Americans should be concerned about the security of their financial institutions, Bessent said: "No, they shouldn't."
paras.zh: 当被问及美国人是否应该担心其金融机构的安全时，贝森特说：“不，他们不应该。”

paras.en: "The patches may cause a glitch," he said, referring to measures banks are taking to safeguard from AI. "I think the American people should think of it as a vaccine; your arm may hurt, you may feel a little bad the next day, but it increases your long-term immunity and resiliency."
paras.zh: “这些补丁可能会导致故障，”他说，指的是银行正在采取的防范人工智能的措施。 “我认为美国人民应该将其视为一种疫苗；你的手臂可能会受伤，第二天你可能会感觉有点难受，但它会增加你的长期免疫力和弹性。”

articles.title: I’ve studied over 200 kids—to avoid raising a people pleaser, ditch 6 parenting habits: It starts in ‘ordinary, well-intentioned moments’

paras.en: We all want to raise children who are kind, respectful and considerate. But sometimes, the very behaviors we praise are the ones teaching our children to put themselves last.
paras.zh: 我们都希望培养出善良、尊重和体贴的孩子。但有时，我们赞扬的行为恰恰教会我们的孩子把自己放在最后。

paras.en: A child who never complains, always agrees and goes out of their way to make others happy might seem like a parent's dream. But what if they've simply learned that being easy to love means trying to please everyone all the time?
paras.zh: 一个从不抱怨、总是同意并竭尽全力让别人快乐的孩子似乎是父母的梦想。但如果他们只是明白，容易被爱意味着一直努力取悦每个人呢？

paras.en: As a conscious parenting coach who's worked with over 200 families, I've seen how people pleasing can begin in the most ordinary, well-intentioned moments at home.
paras.zh: 作为一名曾与 200 多个家庭合作过的有意识的育儿教练，我亲眼目睹了如何从家里最普通、最善意的时刻开始取悦人们。

paras.en: Here are six parenting habits worth reconsidering.
paras.zh: 以下是值得重新考虑的六个养育习惯。

paras.en: We love telling our children how easygoing they are, especially when they rarely complain or make demands. But when being easy earns our approval, children may start believing their needs are a burden and their feelings are better kept to themselves.
paras.zh: 我们喜欢告诉孩子他们是多么随和，尤其是当他们很少抱怨或提出要求时。但是，当轻松赢得我们的认可时，孩子们可能会开始认为他们的需求是一种负担，他们的感受最好保留在自己身上。

paras.en: What to do instead: Make room for your child's disappointment, frustration and disagreement, even when it's inconvenient. They need to know they don't have to be happy or agreeable to be accepted by you.
paras.zh: 该怎么做：为孩子的失望、沮丧和分歧腾出空间，即使这不方便。他们需要知道他们不必高兴或同意才能被你接受。

paras.en: When children question our decisions, it's tempting to respond with "Don't talk back" or "Because I said so." But when we repeatedly shut down their opinions, we may be teaching them that having a voice comes at the cost of a connection with us.
paras.zh: 当孩子质疑我们的决定时，他们很容易会说“不要顶嘴”或“因为我就是这么说的”。但当我们一再拒绝他们的意见时，我们可能会告诉他们，拥有发言权是以牺牲与我们的联系为代价的。

paras.en: What to do instead: Separate disrespectful behavior from differences in perspective. You can say, "You don't have to agree with me. I want to understand what you think."
paras.zh: 该怎么做：将不尊重的行为与观点差异分开。你可以说：“你不必同意我的观点。我想了解你的想法。”

paras.en: Statements that start with "After everything I've done for you…" may seem harmless in the moment, but they can leave children feeling responsible for their parents' emotional well-being.
paras.zh: 以“我为你做了一切之后……”开头的陈述在当下看来可能无害，但它们可以让孩子感到对父母的情感健康负有责任。

paras.en: When children hear this sentiment after misbehaving, they may become more concerned with how to make us feel better instead of thinking about what they did wrong. And they can begin confusing being good with keeping other people happy.
paras.zh: 当孩子在行为不当后听到这种情绪时，他们可能会更加关心如何让我们感觉好一点，而不是思考他们做错了什么。他们可能会开始混淆做好事和让别人快乐。

paras.en: What to do instead: Address your child's behavior without making them feel guilty for disappointing you. Children need to learn to take responsibility for their actions, not for managing their parents' emotions.
paras.zh: 该怎么做：解决孩子的行为，不要让他们因为让你失望而感到内疚。孩子需要学会为自己的行为负责，而不是管理父母的情绪。

paras.en: We praise children for sharing, compromising and letting others have their way. But when self-sacrifice is consistently celebrated, children may begin to believe that being a good person means putting themselves last.
paras.zh: 我们赞扬孩子们分享、妥协和让别人为所欲为。但当自我牺牲受到持续赞扬时，孩子们可能会开始相信，做一个好人意味着把自己放在最后。

paras.en: What to do instead: Teach your child that kindness doesn't require self-sacrifice. Let them know it's okay to opt out, express what they want or choose not to share something. Someone else's disappointment doesn't automatically mean they've done something wrong.
paras.zh: 该怎么做：告诉你的孩子善良不需要自我牺牲。让他们知道可以选择退出、表达自己的想法或选择不分享某些内容。别人的失望并不意味着他们做错了事。

paras.en: We teach children to say "please," "thank you" and "sorry," but how often do we teach them that they're allowed to say "no"?
paras.zh: 我们教孩子们说“请”、“谢谢”和“抱歉”，但我们多久教他们一次可以说“不”呢？

paras.en: When children are expected to hug relatives, share everything or agree in order to avoid offending someone, they may learn that other people's comfort matters more than their own.
paras.zh: 当孩子们被要求拥抱亲戚、分享一切或同意以避免冒犯某人时，他们可能会知道别人的舒适比自己的舒适更重要。

paras.en: What to do instead: Let your child know they can disagree with an adult, decline a hug or express a different opinion without being impolite or disrespectful. Respect means treating others with consideration, not automatically doing what they want.
paras.zh: 该怎么做：让您的孩子知道他们可以不同意成人的意见、拒绝拥抱或表达不同的意见，而不会表现出不礼貌或不尊重。尊重意味着体贴地对待他人，而不是自动做他们想做的事。

paras.en: Children notice when we say yes even though we're overwhelmed, apologize for things that aren't our fault or avoid difficult conversations because we don't want to upset anyone.
paras.zh: 孩子们会注意到，当我们在不知所措的情况下说“是”时，会为不是我们的错的事情道歉，或者避免困难的谈话，因为我们不想让任何人感到不安。

paras.en: We can tell our children to stand up for themselves all day long, but if they watch us constantly abandon our own needs to keep the peace, they'll learn something very different.
paras.zh: 我们可以告诉我们的孩子整天为自己挺身而出，但如果他们看到我们不断放弃自己的需要来维持和平，他们会学到一些非常不同的东西。

paras.en: What to do instead: Let your children see you set boundaries, express your needs and respectfully disappoint people when necessary. Show them that saying no doesn't make someone selfish and that healthy relationships can withstand disagreement.
paras.zh: 该怎么做：让你的孩子看到你设定了界限，表达了你的需求，并在必要时以尊重的方式让别人失望。向他们表明，说“不”并不会使人变得自私，健康的关系可以经受住分歧。

paras.en: Raising a confident child means teaching them that being kind and caring for others doesn't have to come at the expense of being themselves. Because the goal isn't to raise a child who's liked by everyone. It's to raise one who doesn't have to lose themselves to be liked.
paras.zh: 培养一个自信的孩子意味着教导他们善良和关心他人并不一定要以牺牲自己为代价。因为我们的目标不是培养一个人人都喜欢的孩子。这是为了培养一个不必为了讨人喜欢而失去自我的人。

paras.en: Reem Raouda is a certified conscious parenting coach, speaker and author dedicated to one core idea: that loving your child and making them feel safe are not the same thing. She is the founder of The Safe Mom and creator of The Safe Mom Masterclass, helping parents raise emotionally healthy children through emotional safety, connection and self-awareness. Find her on Instagram.
paras.zh: Reem Raouda 是一位经过认证的有意识的育儿教练、演讲家和作家，致力于一个核心理念：爱你的孩子和让他们感到安全不是一回事。她是“安全妈妈”的创始人和“安全妈妈大师班”的创始人，帮助父母通过情绪安全、联系和自我意识来培养情绪健康的孩子。在 Instagram 上找到她。

articles.title: Employees at Eric Trump-backed robot startup lose health benefits as company's cash crunch deepens

paras.en: Employees at Foundation Future Industries were told that their health benefits through administrator Rippling have been terminated, according to a memo obtained by CNBC, adding to mounting signs of financial distress at the humanoid robot startup advised and backed by Eric Trump.
paras.zh: 根据 CNBC 获得的一份备忘录，未来工业基金会的员工被告知，他们通过管理员 Rippling 获得的健康福利已被终止，这加剧了这家由埃里克·特朗普 (Eric Trump) 建议和支持的人形机器人初创公司陷入财务困境的迹象。

paras.en: Foundation told staff in a Friday evening email that they'd be offered coverage through COBRA, the federal law that generally lets workers temporarily keep their health insurance after losing benefits by paying the full premium out of pocket.
paras.zh: 基金会在周五晚上的一封电子邮件中告诉员工，他们将通过 COBRA 获得保险，这是一项联邦法律，通常允许工人在失去福利后通过自付费用全额保费来暂时保留健康保险。

paras.en: "Because our last pay run through Rippling was in October, they have ended our benefits with them retroactive to October," a Foundation human resources manager said in the memo. "COBRA will be offered to all employees to cover November."
paras.zh: “由于我们最后一次通过 Rippling 支付工资是在 10 月份，因此他们终止了我们的福利，并追溯至 10 月份，”基金会人力资源经理在备忘录中表示。 “COBRA 将在 11 月份向所有员工提供。”

paras.en: Foundation has garnered headlines for the bold claims that co-founder Sankaet Pathak — whose previous startup collapsed in 2024 — has made about his robots and their potential use in war zones. Employees were last paid on Oct. 15, and some inside the company are angry at Pathak for a $4.6 million loan he took from his company last year, CNBC reported earlier this month.
paras.zh: Foundation 因其联合创始人 Sankaet Pathak（其上一家初创公司于 2024 年倒闭）关于他的机器人及其在战区的潜在用途的大胆声明而登上了头条。据 CNBC 本月早些时候报道，员工最后一次领取工资是在 10 月 15 日，公司内部的一些人对帕塔克去年从公司借了 460 万美元的贷款感到愤怒。

paras.en: A Foundation spokesman didn't immediately respond to an email or phone call seeking comment.
paras.zh: 基金会发言人没有立即回复寻求置评的电子邮件或电话。

paras.en: In the staff memo, Foundation blamed Rippling for the disruption to health coverage. The startup also said it would reimburse COBRA premiums paid by workers and that it was onboarding a new benefits provider.
paras.zh: 在员工备忘录中，基金会指责 Ripple 造成了医疗保险的中断。该初创公司还表示，将偿还员工支​​付的 COBRA 保费，并正在聘请新的福利提供商。

paras.en: But employees, especially those whose family members are undergoing treatment for medical ailments, worry the company won't have funds to reimburse workers or reinstate coverage, people with direct knowledge of the situation said.
paras.zh: 但知情人士表示，员工们，尤其是那些有家人正在接受疾病治疗的员工，担心公司没有资金来报销员工的医疗费用或恢复保险。

paras.en: In a statement to CNBC, Rippling indicated it was Foundation's failure to pay for its employee benefits that led to the change: "If a client enrolled in Rippling's [Professional Employer Organization] is unable to meet their payroll and benefits obligations for multiple months, they will first receive a warning and if not met, they are terminated."
paras.zh: Rippling 在给 CNBC 的一份声明中表示，正是 Foundation 未能支付员工福利才导致了这一变化：“如果加入 Rippling 的[专业雇主组织]的客户连续几个月无法履行工资和福利义务，他们将首先收到警告，如果不履行，他们将被解雇。”

paras.en: Foundation has been seeking a bridge loan to repay employees after its financial woes began in August. It has been in talks with three or four venture capital firms, including existing investor Tribe Capital, Pathak has told employees, according to people familiar with the situation, who asked to remain unnamed because they were not authorized to speak publicly and feared retaliation. Tribe didn't immediately return a request for comment.
paras.zh: 自八月份开始出现财务困境后，基金会一直在寻求过桥贷款来偿还员工。据知情人士透露，帕塔克告诉员工，该公司已与三四家风险投资公司进行谈判，其中包括现有投资者 Tribe Capital。员工要求匿名，因为他们无权公开发言并担心遭到报复。部落没有立即回复置评请求。

paras.en: The bridge loan would help the company survive until a possible $150 million investment from South Korean conglomerate Base Group lands as early as December or January, Pathak has told employees, the people said.
paras.zh: 知情人士称，帕塔克告诉员工，这笔过桥贷款将帮助该公司生存下去，直到韩国企业集团 Base Group 最早可能在 12 月或 1 月获得 1.5 亿美元的投资。

paras.en: Base confirmed to Reuters in recent days that it was considering an investment, but the funding has not been finalized.
paras.zh: Base最近几天向路透社证实，它正在考虑一项投资，但资金尚未最终确定。

paras.en: The potential investment would deepen business ties between the Trump family and the South Korean conglomerate, an aluminum producer also known for real estate and hospitality projects.
paras.zh: 这项潜在投资将加深特朗普家族与韩国企业集团之间的商业联系，该企业是一家铝生产商，也以房地产和酒店项目而闻名。

paras.en: Base paid the Trump Organization $2 million in 2025, according to a New York Times article, drawing scrutiny from Democratic senators over conflict-of-interest concerns. Base has also pursued other business relationships with the Trump Organization, including a Trump-branded golf course in South Korea.
paras.zh: 据《纽约时报》一篇文章报道，Base 于 2025 年向特朗普集团支付了 200 万美元，此举因利益冲突问题而受到民主党参议员的审查。 Base 还寻求与特朗普集团建立其他业务关系，包括在韩国建立特朗普品牌的高尔夫球场。

paras.en: Eric Trump, who has invested in Foundation and was given the title of chief strategy advisor, didn't immediately respond to a CNBC email seeking comment.
paras.zh: 投资了 Foundation 并被授予首席战略顾问头衔的埃里克·特朗普 (Eric Trump) 没有立即回复 CNBC 寻求置评的电子邮件。

paras.en: The prospect of employees having to pay for their own health coverage comes as many are already drawing down savings to cover living expenses. With another scheduled payday approaching on Nov. 30, workers are facing a third straight pay cycle without income.
paras.zh: 由于许多员工已经动用储蓄来支付生活费用，因此员工可能必须自己支付医疗保险费用。随着 11 月 30 日另一个预定发薪日的临近，工人们将面临连续第三个没有收入的发薪周期。

paras.en: Many are actively interviewing for other jobs, and attendance at the company's San Francisco headquarters has fallen sharply, according to people familiar.
paras.zh: 据知情人士透露，许多人正在积极面试其他工作，而该公司旧金山总部的出席人数急剧下降。

paras.en: Frustration has boiled over into distrust of Pathak's leadership for some employees, while others hope Pathak can secure funding to repay workers and bring the company back to financial health. In conversations and memos, Pathak says that he is highly invested in securing Foundation's future, the people said.
paras.zh: 一些员工对帕塔克的领导力感到沮丧，而另一些员工则希望帕塔克能够获得资金来偿还工人的工资，并使公司恢复财务健康。知情人士称，帕塔克在谈话和备忘录中表示，他为确保基金会的未来投入了大量资金。

paras.en: Despite the firm's shaky finances, Foundation continued to hire for open roles until recently and some new workers have never been fully paid, said the people.
paras.zh: 知情人士称，尽管该公司财务状况不稳定，但直到最近，基金会仍在继续招聘空缺职位，而且一些新员工从未拿到全额工资。

paras.en: To keep employees from leaving before a possible Base Group investment, Pathak has floated the idea of offering workers equity in the startup, the people said.
paras.zh: 知情人士称，为了防止员工在 Base Group 可能投资之前离职，帕塔克提出了向员工提供初创公司股权的想法。

paras.en: At the same time, human resources staff have warned workers against taking legal action with California to recover their wages, saying that any employees who file complaints with the state would be dismissed, the people said.
paras.zh: 知情人士称，与此同时，人力资源工作人员警告工人不要向加州采取法律行动追回工资，称任何向该州提出投诉的员工都将被解雇。

paras.en: Following a Nov. 14 CNBC report detailing the missed payrolls and a $4.6 million loan Pathak took from the startup in 2025, the chief executive addressed the issue in an all-hands meeting, according to the people.
paras.zh: 据知情人士透露，在 11 月 14 日 CNBC 报道详细介绍了帕塔克错过的工资和 2025 年从这家初创公司获得的 460 万美元贷款后，这位首席执行官在一次全体会议上解决了这个问题。

paras.en: Pathak defended the arrangement by telling workers that he had plowed his own money into the startup and takes only a nominal salary, the people said.
paras.zh: 知情人士称，帕塔克为这一安排进行了辩护，他告诉工人们，他是自己掏钱投资这家初创公司的，只拿象征性的工资。

paras.en: The co-founder also told employees who were in dire financial straits to contact human resources for help covering personal bills, the people added.
paras.zh: 知情人士补充说，这位联合创始人还告诉陷入严重财务困境的员工联系人力资源部门寻求个人账单方面的帮助。

paras.en: "I'm burning through savings just to afford my apartment," one employee told CNBC. "It's extremely unfortunate we're in this situation."
paras.zh: 一名员工告诉 CNBC：“为了买一套公寓，我花光了积蓄。” “我们处于这种情况非常不幸。”

articles.title: Listen to the sounds of a baby star as it explodes into life

paras.en: The nominations for the upcoming Grammy awards may be in, but the stars we’re listening to are even bigger than Olivia Rodrigo and Bruno Mars.
paras.zh: 即将到来的格莱美奖提名可能已经出炉，但我们正在聆听的明星甚至比奥利维亚·罗德里戈和布鲁诺·马尔斯还要大。

paras.en: This week, NASA released an album created from observations of baby stars across the galaxy performed by the Chandra X-ray Observatory. The album includes four sonifications of actively forming stars in which data are mapped to sounds, turning stellar formation into a musical journey.
paras.zh: 本周，美国宇航局发布了一张专辑，该专辑是根据钱德拉 X 射线天文台对整个星系的婴儿恒星的观测而制作的。这张专辑包括四个活跃形成的恒星的声音化过程，其中数据被映射到声音，将恒星的形成变成一次音乐之旅。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: Stars are almost constantly forming and dying in Messier 82, which is full of hot gas from the explosions of young, giant stars. X-ray data are captured by high-frequency sounds here, and infrared can be heard as a low drone sound. In between those pitches, visible light is mapped to different musical sounds.
paras.zh: Messier 82 中的恒星几乎不断地形成和死亡，这里充满了年轻巨星爆炸产生的炽热气体。 X 射线数据在这里通过高频声音捕获，而红外线则可以作为低沉的无人机声音听到。在这些音高之间，可见光被映射到不同的音乐声音。

paras.en: Just below the Orion constellation’s belt, more than 1,000 young stars twinkle in this sonification. Even the dust and gas in an infrared image are converted to sound as low musical notes and distorted strings here.
paras.zh: 就在猎户座的腰带下方，有 1000 多颗年轻恒星在这种可听化的声音中闪烁。甚至红外图像中的灰尘和气体在这里也被转换为声音，如低音音符和扭曲的弦乐。

paras.en: In the Carina Nebula’s sonification, individual baby stars each get their own string sound, and other instruments reflect the mountainous shape of the galactic region.
paras.zh: 在船底座星云的声音化过程中，每一颗新生恒星都会发出自己的弦乐声音，而其他乐器则反映了银河地区的山脉形状。

paras.en: Consider this the emo track, with dark dust clouds bringing silence in the middle of the song. Beyond that, young stars and a variety of dust observations create an eerie sound experience.
paras.zh: 将此视为情绪歌曲，黑色的尘埃云在歌曲中间带来了沉默。除此之外，年轻的恒星和各种尘埃观测创造了一种怪异的声音体验。

paras.en: Great science journalism requires human expertise, time, effort and creativity. And it costs money. That’s why I and the journalists here at Scientific American hope you’ll join our community.
paras.zh: 伟大的科学新闻需要人类的专业知识、时间、努力和创造力。而且这需要花钱。这就是为什么我和《科学美国人》的记者希望您加入我们的社区。

paras.en: Jeanna Bryner, Editor in Chief, Scientific American
paras.zh: Jeanna Bryner，《科学美国人》主编

articles.title: Quantum physics can now prove where you really are

paras.en: Your “bank” is texting again: You’ve been hacked, and you need to send your information over immediately. You’re 99 percent sure it’s a scam. It’s the other 1 percent that keeps your thumb hovering over the reply button. Nothing on your screen can tell you whether the sender is who—or where—they claim to be.
paras.zh: 你的“银行”再次发短信：你被黑客入侵了，你需要立即发送你的信息。您 99% 确定这是一个骗局。剩下的 1% 会让你的拇指悬停在回复按钮上。屏幕上没有任何内容可以告诉您发件人是否是他们声称的人或地点。

paras.en: Physicists now have a way to determine the “where,” at least in the lab. In a new experiment led by the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) and described in Nature on Wednesday, researchers confirmed someone’s location by having them catch a photon fired right at them through a fiber-optic cable.
paras.zh: 物理学家现在有办法确定“在哪里”，至少在实验室里是这样。在美国国家标准与技术研究所 (NIST) 领导的一项新实验中，研究人员通过让某人捕捉通过光纤电缆直接发射的光子来确认某人的位置，该实验于周三在《自然》杂志上进行了描述。

paras.en: See, a vault can keep a physical object in its place, and cryptography is pretty good at showing digital information is what it claims to be. Bridging the gap between the digital and physical is much harder. A password can be cracked, an identity can be faked, and even security camera footage shipped over the internet can be spoofed. Location falls into the same gap, which is how a scammer on another continent can pass for bank,
paras.zh: 看，金库可以将物理对象保存在其位置，而密码学非常擅长显示数字信息，正如它所声称的那样。弥合数字和物理之间的差距要困难得多。密码可以被破解，身份可以被伪造，甚至通过互联网传输的安全摄像机镜头也可以被欺骗。位置也属于同样的差距，这就是另一个大陆的骗子可以冒充银行的方式，

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: The NIST team found its answer in quantum physics. Quantum information, like the polarization of the fired photon’s electric field, obeys different rules than the bits and code that make up standard computer communications. For instance, “They can’t be copied, so they have to be measured at one location,” says Krister Shalm, a NIST physicist who led the experiment.
paras.zh: NIST 团队在量子物理学中找到了答案。量子信息，例如发射光子电场的偏振，遵循与构成标准计算机通信的比特和代码不同的规则。例如，领导这项实验的 NIST 物理学家 Krister Shalm 说：“它们无法复制，因此必须在一个位置进行测量。”

paras.en: A photon that can’t be copied can still be intercepted, though, and measured somewhere else. So the researchers built two stations on NIST’s Boulder campus nearly 200 meters apart and put the person in question somewhere in between. One station sent the photon down the fiber, and both fired off random bits dictating how to measure it. Then they timed how long it took the person to catch the photon, measure it and send back a response to both stations. “By measuring that round trip time from when they sent the bits to when they got the answer, they can actually localize where that signal had to have come from,” says Shalm.
paras.zh: 不过，无法复制的光子仍然可以被拦截，并在其他地方进行测量。因此，研究人员在 NIST 博尔德校区建立了两个相距近 200 米的站，并将受调查者安置在两者之间。一个站将光子沿着光纤发送，两个站都发射随机位来指示如何测量它。然后他们计算了这个人捕获光子所需的时间，测量它并向两个站发回响应。 “通过测量从发送比特到得到答案的往返时间，他们实际上可以定位信号的来源，”沙尔姆说。

paras.en: Shalm and his collaborators created a sort of quantum echolocation, pinging signals from different locations to triangulate a position. Only the photon sender and the pinpointee need any sort of quantum technology. So the other “ear”—as in, the average person’s computer—could check locations without any quantum capability. The hope is that a network of optical fiber could let anyone prove where they are to anyone else in the same city.
paras.zh: 沙姆和他的合作者创造了一种量子回声定位技术，通过从不同位置发出 ping 信号来对位置进行三角测量。只有光子发送者和精确接收者需要某种量子技术。因此，另一只“耳朵”——就像普通人的计算机一样——可以在没有任何量子能力的情况下检查位置。希望光纤网络可以让任何人向同一城市的其他人证明自己所在的位置。

paras.en: That idea has excited quantum researchers for years. “I’ve been telling everyone for the last two years that this is my new obsession,” says Henry Yuen, an associate professor of computer science at Columbia University. He says he used to be very skeptical of the need for this kind of work. The rise of AI agents and AI-enabled scamming changed his mind, and making sure someone actually is where they say they are strikes him as urgent.
paras.zh: 这个想法多年来一直让量子研究人员兴奋不已。 “过去两年我一直告诉大家，这是我新的痴迷，”哥伦比亚大学计算机科学副教授 Henry Yuen 说。他说他曾经对这种工作的必要性非常怀疑。人工智能代理和人工智能诈骗的兴起改变了他的想法，确保某人确实在他们所说的地方对他来说是紧迫的。

paras.en: The experiment isn’t scalable yet, though. NIST cautions that real-world use may be more than a decade away. Yuen believes the holdup is mainly a matter of engineering and building out quantum-friendly networks. “We went from zero to one this year with this NIST experiment,” he says. “It’ll take a few years, but it seems like this is going to happen.”
paras.zh: 不过，该实验还无法扩展。 NIST 警告说，实际应用可能还需要十多年的时间。袁认为，阻碍主要是工程和构建量子友好网络的问题。 “今年我们通过 NIST 实验从零到一，”他说。 “这需要几年的时间，但看起来这将会发生。”

paras.en: Others are less bullish on such a quick timeline. George Siopsis, a physics professor at the University of Tennessee, Knoxville, notes that the scheme only works if whoever sends the photon is much more technically advanced than any would-be spoofer. He also warns that the speedy photons may be harder to measure precisely outside a lab. After all, he says, “Light travels at the speed of light.”
paras.zh: 其他人则不太看好这么快的时间表。诺克斯维尔田纳西大学物理学教授乔治·西奥普斯指出，只有发送光子的技术比任何潜在的欺骗者都先进得多，该计划才有效。他还警告说，快速光子可能更难在实验室外精确测量。毕竟，他说，“光以光速传播。”

paras.en: Quantum technology usually makes headlines for its promises of faster computers. Shalm’s photon suggests it could also make lying about your location a lot harder. And it would be a relief to know that the next text from your bank actually came from, well, the bank.
paras.zh: 量子技术通常因其承诺更快的计算机而成为头条新闻。沙姆的光子表明，它也可能会让你的位置谎言变得更加困难。如果知道您的银行发来的下一条短信实际上来自银行，那将是一种解脱。

articles.title: Erectile dysfunction drug could hold promise for Alzheimer’s disease

paras.en: A drug developed to treat erectile dysfunction might seem an unlikely treatment for Alzheimer’s disease. But researchers are increasingly interested in whether medicines such as Viagra could also help protect the brain.
paras.zh: 一种用于治疗勃起功能障碍的药物似乎不太可能治疗阿尔茨海默病。但研究人员越来越感兴趣的是伟哥等药物是否也有助于保护大脑。

paras.en: These drugs affect blood flow and other processes that may play a role in brain health. An experimental drug called AR1001 has produced encouraging results in a large international clinical trial.
paras.zh: 这些药物会影响血流和其他可能对大脑健康发挥作用的过程。一种名为 AR1001 的实验药物在一项大型国际临床试验中取得了令人鼓舞的结果。

paras.en: In one group of people with early Alzheimer’s, the drug was reported to slow the worsening of symptoms by 31% over a year, compared with a placebo.
paras.zh: 据报道，在一组早期阿尔茨海默病患者中，与安慰剂相比，该药物在一年内可将症状恶化速度减缓 31%。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: AriBio, a South Korean biotechnology company, announced the results at the 19th Clinical Trials on Alzheimer’s Disease conference in Boston, US. A full scientific paper, reviewed by other researchers, has not yet been published.
paras.zh: 韩国生物技术公司AriBio在美国波士顿举行的第19届阿尔茨海默病临床试验会议上公布了这一结果。经其他研究人员审阅的完整科学论文尚未发表。

paras.en: The phase three trial—the final phase of testing in humans—involved 1,535 people with early Alzheimer’s in 13 countries. Participants took either 30mg of AR1001 or a placebo every day for a year.
paras.zh: 第三阶段试验（人体测试的最后阶段）涉及 13 个国家的 1,535 名早期阿尔茨海默病患者。参与者在一年内每天服用 30 毫克 AR1001 或安慰剂。

paras.en: Researchers measured changes in memory, thinking and everyday activities. They looked at two groups: everyone who took part in the trial and a smaller group of 604 people who were not taking other Alzheimer’s medicines to ease their symptoms, such as donepezil or memantine.
paras.zh: 研究人员测量了记忆、思维和日常活动的变化。他们研究了两组：所有参加试验的人，以及一小部分 604 名未服用其他阿尔茨海默病药物（如多奈哌齐或美金刚）来缓解症状的人。

paras.en: Only this smaller group saw a 31 percent reduction in worsening symptoms. Across the whole trial, AR1001 did not produce reliable benefits.
paras.zh: 只有这个较小的群体的症状恶化程度减少了 31%。在整个试验过程中，AR1001 并未产生可靠的益处。

paras.en: How could erectile dysfunction drugs affect the brain?
paras.zh: 勃起功能障碍药物如何影响大脑？

paras.en: Erectile dysfunction drugs work by blocking an enzyme that normally breaks down a chemical messenger – called cGMP – in the body. This allows cGMP to build up, helping the muscles around blood vessels relax. The vessels widen, allowing more blood to flow through them. This is how the drugs help treat erectile dysfunction.
paras.zh: 勃起功能障碍药物通过阻断体内通常分解化学信使（称为 cGMP）的酶来发挥作用。这使得 cGMP 得以积累，帮助血管周围的肌肉放松。血管变宽，允许更多的血液流过它们。这就是药物帮助治疗勃起功能障碍的方式。

paras.en: The same chemical messenger also helps brain cells communicate with each other. Researchers think that increasing its levels could help brain cells survive and maintain the connections they need to share information.
paras.zh: 同样的化学信使还可以帮助脑细胞相互沟通。研究人员认为，增加其水平可以帮助脑细胞生存并维持共享信息所需的连接。

paras.en: These connections are essential for learning and memory. Alzheimer’s gradually damages them, making it harder to remember things and think clearly. Researchers hope that AR1001 might help protect some of these connections and slow the damage caused by the disease.
paras.zh: 这些联系对于学习和记忆至关重要。阿尔茨海默氏症逐渐损害它们，使人更难记住事情和清晰思考。研究人员希望 AR1001 可能有助于保护其中一些连接并减缓疾病造成的损害。

paras.en: However, this is still a theory. The clinical trial does not show that these biological changes explain the reported benefits in people.
paras.zh: 然而，这仍然是一个理论。临床试验并未表明这些生物学变化可以解释所报道的对人类的益处。

paras.en: Some laboratory and animal studies support the idea. In a 2022 study, mice with features of Alzheimer’s disease performed better in memory tests after receiving AR1001. The treatment also reduced levels of amyloid-beta and abnormal tau, two proteins linked to Alzheimer’s.
paras.zh: 一些实验室和动物研究支持这个想法。在 2022 年的一项研究中，患有阿尔茨海默病特征的小鼠在接受 AR1001 后在记忆测试中表现更好。该治疗还降低了β-淀粉样蛋白和异常tau蛋白的水平，这两种蛋白质与阿尔茨海默病有关。

paras.en: Other experimental researchin mice has found that AR1001 can increase levels of cGMP and a protein that helps brain cells survive. However, results in animals do not always translate into benefits for humans.
paras.zh: 其他针对小鼠的实验研究发现，AR1001 可以提高 cGMP 和一种有助于脑细胞存活的蛋白质的水平。然而，动物身上的结果并不总是转化为对人类的好处。

paras.en: Interest in this family of drugs has also grown following research in people. A 2024 studyfollowed more than 269,000 men with erectile dysfunction. It found that men prescribed these drugs were 18% less likely to be diagnosed with Alzheimer’s than men who were not prescribed them.
paras.zh: 在人体研究之后，人们对这一类药物的兴趣也随之增加。 2024 年的一项研究对超过 269,000 名患有勃起功能障碍的男性进行了跟踪调查。研究发现，服用这些药物的男性被诊断出患有阿尔茨海默病的可能性比未服用这些药物的男性低 18%。

paras.en: But this was an observational study, which means it cannot show that the drugs themselves reduced the risk of Alzheimer’s. The two groups may have differed in other ways that influenced the results.
paras.zh: 但这是一项观察性研究，这意味着它无法证明药物本身可以降低患阿尔茨海默病的风险。这两个群体可能在影响结果的其他方面存在差异。

paras.en: The relationship between erectile dysfunction and Alzheimer’s is complicated. Erectile dysfunction can be associated with conditions such as diabetes, high blood pressure and heart disease, which can damage blood vessels. These same conditions are also linked to poorer brain health and a higher risk of dementia.
paras.zh: 勃起功能障碍和阿尔茨海默氏症之间的关系很复杂。勃起功能障碍可能与糖尿病、高血压和心脏病等疾病有关，这些疾病会损害血管。这些相同的情况也与较差的大脑健康状况和较高的痴呆风险有关。

paras.en: This means that some of the apparent link between erectile dysfunction, its treatments and dementia could be down to shared risk factors affecting blood vessels, rather than a direct effect of the drugs.
paras.zh: 这意味着勃起功能障碍及其治疗和痴呆之间的一些明显联系可能归因于影响血管的共同危险因素，而不是药物的直接作用。

paras.en: Erectile dysfunction drugs are not an established treatment for Alzheimer’s, and nothing in these results suggests people should take them to protect their memory.
paras.zh: 勃起功能障碍药物并不是阿尔茨海默氏症的既定治疗方法，这些结果中没有任何内容表明人们应该服用这些药物来保护他们的记忆。

paras.en: The latest trial does, however, keep alive an interesting possibility: that drugs that improve blood flow and help brain cells communicate might also slow the damage caused by Alzheimer’s.
paras.zh: 然而，最新的试验确实保留了一个有趣的可能性：改善血液流动和帮助脑细胞交流的药物也可能减缓阿尔茨海默氏症造成的损害。

paras.en: Whether this is the case will depend on the full trial results and further research in people, including studies looking at why the apparent benefit was seen only among those not taking other Alzheimer’s medicines.
paras.zh: 情况是否如此，将取决于完整的试验结果和对人体的进一步研究，包括研究为什么只有那些不服用其他阿尔茨海默氏症药物的人才能看到明显的益处。

paras.en: This article was first published by The Conversation. Read the original article here.
paras.zh: 本文最初由《对话》发表。在这里阅读原文。

articles.title: The libido drug women want is testosterone
articles.author: Jamie Ducharme

paras.en: These days, Jessica Yih spends a lot of time talking to women about testosterone. Interest is “coming from all directions,” says the University of California, Irvine Health urologist. A major source: women who hope testosterone can boost the female libido. Only about a decade ago, women looking for libido treatments had few medical options — even though women of all ages struggle with low sexual desire.
paras.zh: 这些天，Jessica Yih 花了很多时间与女性谈论睾丸激素。加州大学欧文分校健康中心的泌尿科医生表示，人们的兴趣“来自四面八方”。主要来源：希望睾丸激素能够增强女性性欲的女性。仅在大约十年前，寻求性欲治疗的女性几乎没有医疗选择——尽管所有年龄段的女性都在与性欲低下作斗争。

paras.en: Some non-hormonal treatments are now available, but the U.S. Food and Drug Administration has yet to approve a female testosterone product, despite years of research suggesting it can boost sexual function and desire among postmenopausal women. Female testosterone products are approved in countries including the United Kingdom and Australia.
paras.zh: 现在已经有了一些非激素治疗方法，但美国食品和药物管理局尚未批准女性睾酮产品，尽管多年的研究表明它可以增强绝经后女性的性功能和性欲。女性睾酮产品在英国和澳大利亚等国家获得批准。

paras.en: Not many studies have looked at testosterone’s effects on libido in premenopausal women, but preliminary data in that area are also promising, according to a 2026 research review in The Journal of Sexual Medicine that Yih coauthored. “I have seen it change people’s lives,” Yih says. The hormone seems to make the female brain more receptive to sexual stimuli; it also promotes physical effects that enhance sexual pleasure, such as increased blood flow to the genitals. Right now, American women interested in these potential benefits have to look for them off-label. But that may change. In September, the FDA held a public meeting on testosterone use among menopausal women, “with the goal of informing future research and potential drug development in this area,” says Kaveeta Vasisht, the FDA’s associate commissioner for women’s health.
paras.zh: 没有多少研究关注睾酮对绝经前女性性欲的影响，但根据 Yih 与人合着的《性医学杂志》2026 年的一篇研究评论，该领域的初步数据也很有希望。 “我看到它改变了人们的生活，”Yih 说。这种激素似乎能让女性大脑更容易接受性刺激。它还可以促进增强性快感的身体效果，例如增加生殖器的血流量。目前，对这些潜在益处感兴趣的美国女性必须在标签外寻找它们。但这可能会改变。今年 9 月，FDA 召开了一次关于更年期女性睾酮使用情况的公开会议，“目的是为该领域的未来研究和潜在药物开发提供信息”，FDA 女性健康副专员 Kaveeta Vasisht 表示。

paras.en: The hormone has a rocky regulatory past. In 2004, an FDA advisory panel unanimously voted against approving a testosterone patch for women, citing a lack of safety data. There are still outstanding questions on that front, Yih says—like how, if at all, long-term use affects risk of conditions such as breast cancer and heart disease. Then, in 2011, a pair of Phase III trials found that testosterone therapy didn’t significantly outperform a placebo — a benchmark the FDA looks for when deciding whether to approve a new drug. That’s not to say testosterone didn’t work, says Tami Rowen, an ob-gyn at UC San Francisco. Rather, it seemed that hype about the hormone was so strong that study participants went in with sky-high expectations, leading even the placebo group to report benefits. The treatment was a “victim of its own success,” Rowen says.
paras.zh: 这种激素的监管历史坎坷。 2004年，FDA顾问小组一致投票反对批准女性睾酮贴片，理由是缺乏安全数据。 Yih 表示，这方面仍然存在一些悬而未决的问题，比如长期使用会如何影响乳腺癌和心脏病等疾病的风险。然后，在 2011 年，两项 III 期试验发现，睾酮疗法并没有明显优于安慰剂——这是 FDA 在决定是否批准新药时寻找的基准。加州大学旧金山分校的妇产科医生塔米·罗文 (Tami Rowen) 表示，这并不是说睾酮不起作用。相反，似乎对这种激素的炒作是如此强烈，以至于研究参与者抱着极高的期望，甚至导致安慰剂组也报告了其好处。罗文说，这种治疗方法是“其自身成功的受害者”。

paras.en: Interest hasn’t let up, though. By one estimate, the U.S. female prescription rate for all uses rose from 0.4 out of every 1,000 women in 2018, to 1.8 out of every 1,000 women in 2026. That’s an increase of nearly 400 percent. With so much buzz, the potential placebo effect remains “the biggest problem with testosterone right now,” Rowen says.
paras.zh: 不过，人们的兴趣并没有减弱。据估计，美国女性所有用途的处方率从 2018 年的每 1,000 名女性 0.4 例上升到 2026 年的每 1,000 名女性 1.8 例。增幅接近 400%。罗文说，尽管如此，潜在的安慰剂效应仍然是“目前睾丸激素的最大问题”。

paras.en: Another outstanding question, Yih says, is whether using testosterone long-term increases the risk of breast cancer and heart disease.
paras.zh: 叶说，另一个悬而未决的问题是长期使用睾酮是否会增加患乳腺癌和心脏病的风险。

paras.en: Women seeking a libido boost do have non-hormonal options. In 2015, the FDA approved Addyi, the first treatment for low libido in premenopausal women. The drug seemingly raises levels of neurotransmitters that promote sexual desire while tamping down those that block it. A competitor, Vyleesi, hit shelves in 2019. Then, last year, regulators expanded Addyi’s use to postmenopausal women younger than 65. An international group of experts, including Rowen, issued recommendations for treating low female libido in 2025 in Sexual Medicine Reviews. Psychological therapies and Addyi are backed by the strongest evidence, the group found.
paras.zh: 寻求增强性欲的女性确实有非激素选择。 2015年，FDA批准了Addyi，这是第一个治疗绝经前女性性欲低下的药物。这种药物似乎会提高促进性欲的神经递质水平，同时抑制那些阻碍性欲的神经递质。其竞争对手 Vyleesi 于 2019 年上架。去年，监管机构将 Addyi 的使用范围扩大到 65 岁以下的绝经后女性。包括 Rowen 在内的国际专家组在《性医学评论》中于 2025 年发布了治疗女性性欲低下的建议。研究小组发现，心理疗法和 Addyi 得到了最有力的证据支持。

paras.en: Rowen currently has her eye on in-development products including Lybrido. The drug, which is slated to enter a Phase III clinical trial in Europe, aims to rev sex drive in the brain and enhance physical arousal. The demand for new treatments is there, Rowen says. “Women deserve better than placebo.”
paras.zh: Rowen 目前关注的是包括 Lybrido 在内的正在开发的产品。该药物计划在欧洲进入 III 期临床试验，旨在加速大脑的性欲并增强身体的兴奋。罗文说，对新疗法的需求是存在的。 “女性应该得到比安慰剂更好的东西。”

articles.title: How do tumors talk to nerves? This scientist is finding out
articles.author: Anna Mattson

paras.en: Sebnem Ece Eksi did a double take. Proteins typically studied in the brain were turning up in prostate cancer cells from high-risk patients. These proteins, called neuronal adhesion molecules, play a key role in the circuitry associated with memory.
paras.zh: Sebnem Ece Eksi 愣了一下。通常在大脑中研究的蛋白质出现在高危患者的前列腺癌细胞中。这些蛋白质被称为神经元粘附分子，在与记忆相关的电路中发挥着关键作用。

paras.en: The finding, made during her Ph.D. days at the University of Illinois Chicago, raised so many questions to which Eksi is still seeking answers. Now at the Oregon Health & Science University in Portland, Eksi has made it her lab’s goal to find out how nervous systems communicate with cancer. What were once two separate fields might be connected more closely than previously thought.
paras.zh: 这一发现是她在攻读博士学位期间做出的。在伊利诺伊大学芝加哥分校的几天里，提出了很多问题，而 Eksi 仍在寻找答案。现在，在波特兰的俄勒冈健康与科学大学，埃克西的实验室目标是找出神经系统如何与癌症沟通。曾经两个独立的领域之间的联系可能比之前想象的更加紧密。

paras.en: “What we’re learning is that tumors are actively communicating with the nervous system,” Eksi says. “In a way, it makes sense to me that a growing tumor in our bodies, in an organ, would be immediately sensed and detected by the nervous system.”
paras.zh: “我们了解到，肿瘤正在与神经系统积极沟通，”埃克西说。 “在某种程度上，对我来说，神经系统会立即感知和检测到我们体内某个器官中不断生长的肿瘤，这是有道理的。”

paras.en: Eksi now plans to test an AI image-based recognition algorithm to identify nerve fibers in human patients. This is exciting, she says, because these nerves aren’t normally visible in patient tumors. But through biopsies, she hopes to map out and observe how the nervous system — which impacts sleep, cognition and pain — changes as cancer progresses. The implications are significant, she says. Could experts use the nervous system to detect cancer early? Can they improve patients’ quality of life?
paras.zh: Eksi 现在计划测试一种基于人工智能图像的识别算法，以识别人类患者的神经纤维。她说，这很令人兴奋，因为这些神经在患者肿瘤中通常不可见。但通过活检，她希望了解并观察影响睡眠、认知和疼痛的神经系统如何随着癌症的进展而变化。她说，其影响是重大的。专家能否利用神经系统早期发现癌症？它们能改善患者的生活质量吗？

paras.en: “This field of cancer neuroscience can change all different stages of cancer diagnosis and treatments,” Eksi says. “It’s growing so quickly, the field itself.”
paras.zh: “癌症神经科学这一领域可以改变癌症诊断和治疗的所有不同阶段，”埃克西说。 “这个领域本身发展得非常快。”

articles.title: How do scientists learn from failure? This researcher has clues
articles.author: Anna Mattson

paras.en: Yian Yin seeks to understand the dynamics of science itself. The computational social scientist is particularly interested in how innovations happen and how they may be accelerated.
paras.zh: 尹彦试图了解科学本身的动态。计算社会科学家对创新如何发生以及如何加速创新特别感兴趣。

paras.en: “I want to understand what the secret sources or recipes of success are,” says Yin, of Cornell University.
paras.zh: “我想了解成功的秘密来源或秘诀是什么，”康奈尔大学的尹说。

paras.en: He applied machine learning techniques to accepted and rejected research proposals to understand how scientists learn from failures. What he found was that scientists fail, and they fail often. Some switched gears after some rejections, but others who continued their research and incorporated feedback found success at a faster rate. Those who changed ideas or scrapped original proposals did not leverage a lot from their experience.
paras.zh: 他将机器学习技术应用于接受和拒绝的研究提案，以了解科学家如何从失败中学习。他发现科学家会失败，而且他们经常失败。有些人在遭到拒绝后改变了方向，但其他人继续研究并吸收反馈，发现成功的速度更快。那些改变想法或放弃最初提案的人并没有充分利用他们的经验。

paras.en: “A group that’s not only failing better and better,” Yin says, “is also failing faster and increasingly faster towards their eventual success.”
paras.zh: 尹说：“一个团队不仅会失败得越来越好，而且失败的速度也会越来越快，最终走向成功。”

paras.en: More recently, Yin has been investigating how generative AI is changing scientific publishing. Journals are receiving more AI-assisted submissions than ever before, which is leading the peer-review process to falter. More seemingly well-written papers that lack substance are getting through, he found. Coming up with large-scale solutions requires looking at the issue in a measurable way, Yin says.
paras.zh: 最近，尹一直在研究生成人工智能如何改变科学出版。期刊收到的人工智能辅助投稿比以往任何时候都多，这导致同行评审过程陷入困境。他发现，更多看似写得很好但缺乏实质内容的论文正在被通过。尹说，提出大规模解决方案需要以可衡量的方式看待问题。

paras.en: “Considering both the technological and social side of scientific ecosystems would be something that’s really beneficial for the ongoing public debate and discussion about how we accelerate science in the age of artificial intelligence,” Yin says.
paras.zh: 尹说：“考虑到科学生态系统的技术和社会方面，对于正在进行的关于如何在人工智能时代加速科学发展的公众辩论和讨论来说，这确实是有益的。”

articles.title: A Physicist Built a Black Hole on a Chip. Then It Started to Leak.
articles.author: Michelle Starr

paras.en: They sit in space, slurping up matter, drawing spacetime around them like a cozy blanket, and firing off powerful jets of near-light-speed plasma.
paras.zh: 它们坐在太空中，吞噬物质，像舒适的毯子一样将时空拉到它们周围，并发射强大的近光速等离子体射流。

paras.en: What they are not especially good at is letting go.
paras.zh: 他们特别不擅长的是放手。

paras.en: But when physicist Antonino Flachi of Keio University in Japan built an analog black hole on a chip, something strange happened at its tiny event horizon – something that, in a real black hole, would be forbidden by the laws of general relativity.
paras.zh: 但是，当日本庆应义塾大学的物理学家安东尼诺·弗拉奇（Antonino Flachi）在芯片上建造了一个模拟黑洞时，在其微小的视界处发生了一些奇怪的事情——在真正的黑洞中，这是广义相对论定律所禁止的。

paras.en: When he poked a hole – metaphorically speaking – the black hole began to leak.
paras.zh: 当他戳一个洞时——打个比方来说——黑洞就开始泄漏。

paras.en: It's an experiment that offers physicists a new tool for probing which properties of black holes are universal – and which might change when the rules of physics do.
paras.zh: 这项实验为物理学家提供了一种新工具，用于探究黑洞的哪些属性是普遍存在的，以及哪些属性可能会随着物理规则的改变而改变。

paras.en: "Digital circuits thus form a reconfigurable class of gravitational analogs," Flachi writes in a preprint (yet to undergo peer review) uploaded to arXiv, "and realize an analog black hole as a cellular automaton."
paras.zh: Flachi 在上传到 arXiv 的预印本（尚未经过同行评审）中写道：“数字电路因此形成了一类可重新配置的引力模拟，并将模拟黑洞实现为细胞自动机。”

paras.en: Their penchant for absorbing light and letting nothing detectable escape from within their event horizons means they're invisible to most of the tools we use for studying the cosmos – telescopes that rely on the electromagnetic spectrum.
paras.zh: 它们喜欢吸收光线，并且不让任何可检测到的东西从其事件视界内逃逸，这意味着我们用于研究宇宙的大多数工具（依赖电磁频谱的望远镜）都看不到它们。

paras.en: However, the mathematics describing the behavior of black holes can be used to build laboratory experiments that replicate some of their properties and behaviors so that we can study what they are capable of.
paras.zh: 然而，描述黑洞行为的数学可用于建立实验室实验，复制黑洞的一些属性和行为，以便我们可以研究它们的能力。

paras.en: Sound waves traveling through a moving fluid can behave in ways very similar to light traveling through the curved spacetime around a black hole. If the fluid flows inward faster than sound can travel outward, the sound waves become trapped, unable to escape the current.
paras.zh: 穿过移动流体的声波的行为方式与穿过黑洞周围弯曲时空的光非常相似。如果流体向内流动的速度快于声音向外传播的速度，声波就会被困住，无法逃脱水流。

paras.en: This creates what physicists call an acoustic black hole.
paras.zh: 这创造了物理学家所说的声学黑洞。

paras.en: But what if you could build an acoustic black hole without all the mess and fuss of speakers, fluids, and currents?
paras.zh: 但是，如果你可以建造一个声学黑洞，而没有扬声器、流体和电流的混乱和大惊小怪呢？

paras.en: This is what Flachi has done, replacing the entire kit and kaboodle with a compact digital circuit.
paras.zh: 这就是 Flachi 所做的，用紧凑的数字电路取代了整个套件和 kaboodle。

paras.en: "We have built an analog black hole out of logic gates," he writes.
paras.zh: “我们用逻辑门建造了一个模拟黑洞，”他写道。

paras.en: "Its horizon is a property not of the wiring but of the state: a closed curve in a lattice of 32-bit words along which the emergent flow carries disturbances inward exactly as fast as they spread outward."
paras.zh: “它的地平线不是布线的属性，而是状态的属性：32 位字格中的一条闭合曲线，沿着该曲线，出现的流向内携带扰动的速度与向外传播的速度完全相同。”

paras.en: He calls his system a 'digital acoustic black hole', a circuit that contains a grid of cells, each storing information as a series of bits – the ones and zeros that form the basis of digital computing. The grid stored a total of around 604 million bits.
paras.zh: 他将他的系统称为“数字声学黑洞”，这是一个包含单元网格的电路，每个单元将信息存储为一系列位——构成数字计算基础的 1 和 0。该网格总共存储了约 6.04 亿比特。

paras.en: At each tick of a clock, logic gates update the information in each cell according to a set of rules based on fluid dynamics, creating the digital equivalent of water flowing inward toward a drain.
paras.zh: 在时钟的每一个滴答声中，逻辑门都会根据一组基于流体动力学的规则更新每个单元中的信息，从而创建相当于水向内流向排水沟的数字等价物。

paras.en: These rules also govern how disturbances travel through the grid. Where the simulated flow carries those disturbances inward as fast as they can travel outward, an acoustic event horizon emerges.
paras.zh: 这些规则还管理干扰如何通过电网传播。当模拟流将这些扰动向内传播的速度与向外传播的速度一样快时，就会出现声学事件视界。

paras.en: Unlike a physical fluid, which can be unpredictable and difficult to control, the precisely defined rules for the digital acoustic black hole make the digital fluid far more controllable. Experiments can even be repeated under identical conditions, right down to the individual bits.
paras.zh: 与不可预测且难以控制的物理流体不同，数字声学黑洞的精确定义规则使数字流体更加可控。实验甚至可以在相同的条件下重复进行，甚至可以重复到各个部分。

paras.en: To test his creation, Flachi measured five properties of the simulated black hole: the stability of its event horizon, the horizon itself, the way disturbances propagate through it, its response to being disturbed (the ringdown), and a phenomenon called superradiance, in which waves can gain energy from a rotating black hole.
paras.zh: 为了测试他的创造，弗拉奇测量了模拟黑洞的五个属性：事件视界的稳定性、视界本身、扰动通过它传播的方式、它对被扰动的响应（振铃）以及一种称为超辐射的现象，在这种现象中，波可以从旋转的黑洞获得能量。

paras.en: It performed brilliantly. The event horizon remained stable for 3 hours, and the circuit demonstrated ringdown and superradiance, consistent with the mathematical predictions.
paras.zh: 它表现出色。事件视界保持稳定3小时，电路呈现衰荡和超辐射现象，与数学预测一致。

paras.en: But then, Flachi got curious. He wanted to know what would happen if he changed one small thing.
paras.zh: 但随后，弗拉奇开始好奇了。他想知道如果他改变一件小事会发生什么。

paras.en: Inside the event horizon, he flipped just one of the system's 604 million bits – and it was as though the black hole had sprung a leak.
paras.zh: 在事件视界内，他只翻转了系统 6.04 亿比特中的一个，就好像黑洞出现了泄漏一样。

paras.en: Flipping the bit created an acoustic disturbance in the black hole. Most of it remained contained beyond the event horizon – as you would expect for something taking place behind that boundary.
paras.zh: 翻转钻头会在黑洞中产生声学干扰。其中大部分仍然包含在事件视界之外——正如你所期望的，在该边界后面发生的事情。

paras.en: But a small fraction of the disturbance escaped, carried by short-wavelength waves that could travel faster than the effective speed of sound in the circuit.
paras.zh: 但一小部分干扰逃脱了，由短波长波携带，这些短波长波的传播速度可能比电路中的有效声速更快。

paras.en: So the event horizon worked as expected for longer waves, but was not quite so impenetrable to shorter ones.
paras.zh: 因此，对于较长的波，事件视界按预期工作，但对于较短的波来说，却并非那么难以穿透。

paras.en: And the deeper inside the horizon Flachi flipped the bit, the less of the disturbance escaped. The leakage diminished exponentially with distance from the boundary.
paras.zh: 弗拉奇将钻头翻转得越深，逃逸的干扰就越少。泄漏随着距边界的距离呈指数减少。

paras.en: This doesn't mean that real black holes have leaky event horizons – but it reveals something important about black hole analogs. The behavior of their horizons isn't necessarily universal, but can depend on the underlying physics of the system in which they emerge.
paras.zh: 这并不意味着真正的黑洞具有泄漏的事件视界，但它揭示了黑洞类似物的一些重要信息。它们的视界行为不一定是普遍的，但可能取决于它们所在系统的底层物理原理。

paras.en: And Flachi's system offers a new way to poke them. He has shown that a functioning black hole analog can be built entirely out of digital logic – one whose underlying rules are precisely known and finely controllable.
paras.zh: Flachi 的系统提供了一种戳它们的新方法。他已经证明，一个功能齐全的黑洞模拟可以完全由数字逻辑构建——其基本规则是精确已知且可精细控制的。

paras.en: This means that it can be used to probe the physics of black hole horizons, and to explore new scenarios that reveal what might be possible if the rules of physics were bent just a teeny tiny iota.
paras.zh: 这意味着它可以用来探测黑洞视界的物理现象，并探索新的场景，揭示如果物理规则发生一点点弯曲可能会发生什么。

paras.en: The paper has not yet been peer-reviewed, but a preprint is available on arXiv.
paras.zh: 该论文尚未经过同行评审，但预印本已在 arXiv 上提供。

articles.title: People Exposed to Sugar Rationing in Early Life Appear Biologically Younger in Their 50s
articles.author: Esra Öz

paras.en: Could the sugar available before birth and in infancy have a connection to our health half a century later?
paras.zh: 半个世纪后，出生前和婴儿期摄入的糖与我们的健康有联系吗？

paras.en: A new study has found that people whose earliest development overlapped with Britain's sugar rationing had blood measurements in their 50s that suggested a younger biological profile.
paras.zh: 一项新的研究发现，那些最早发育与英国糖配给重叠的人在 50 多岁时进行的血液测量表明他们的生物学特征更年轻。

paras.en: The research explores a connection between nutrition during a period we can't remember and our health as adults.
paras.zh: 这项研究探讨了我们不记得的一段时期的营养与我们成年后的健康之间的联系。

paras.en: To trace that connection, researchers turned to a policy that ended in September 1953. Until then, families in Britain could buy only limited amounts of sugar. When household sugar restrictions lifted, consumption rose sharply.
paras.zh: 为了追踪这种联系，研究人员求助于 1953 年 9 月结束的一项政策。在那之前，英国家庭只能购买有限数量的糖。当家庭食糖限制解除后，消费量急剧上升。

paras.en: Children born just a few years apart therefore encountered different nutritional environments at the start of their lives.
paras.zh: 因此，出生时间相隔几年的孩子在生命之初会遇到不同的营养环境。

paras.en: The study of 54,201 adults, published in Nature Communications, found that the longer rationing extended from development before birth into infancy, the greater the difference in biological age.
paras.zh: 这项针对 54,201 名成年人的研究发表在《自然通讯》上，发现从出生前的发育到婴儿期的配给时间越长，生物年龄的差异就越大。

paras.en: In the longest-exposed group, biological age relative to the age-expected value was around five months lower than in unexposed participants. This group also had lower risks of cataracts and chronic kidney disease later in life.
paras.zh: 在暴露时间最长的组中，相对于预期年龄的生物年龄比未暴露的参与者低约五个月。该群体在以后的生活中患白内障和慢性肾病的风险也较低。

paras.en: The historical change offered a rare opportunity to investigate links between early nutrition and adult health. The team could use a national shift in sugar availability without asking families to recall meals eaten decades earlier.
paras.zh: 这一历史性变化为研究早期营养与成人健康之间的联系提供了难得的机会。研究小组可以利用全国范围内糖供应量的变化，而无需要求家庭回忆几十年前吃过的饭菜。

paras.en: Led by ophthalmology researchers Jason C. Yam and Li Jia Chen at the Chinese University of Hong Kong, the team examined information from UK Biobank, a large health database.
paras.zh: 由香港中文大学眼科研究人员 Jason C. Yam 和 Li Jia Chen 领导的研究小组检查了大型健康数据库英国生物银行的信息。

paras.en: They selected participants born in Britain between October 1951 and March 1956, comparing those exposed to rationing during early development with those conceived after restrictions ended.
paras.zh: 他们选择了 1951 年 10 月至 1956 年 3 月出生于英国的参与者，将那些在早期发育期间受到配给的参与者与那些在限制结束后受孕的参与者进行了比较。

paras.en: Their focus was the first 1,000 days, from conception to around a child's second birthday. During this period, organs develop and systems controlling energy use and responses to hormones take shape. Nutritional conditions at this stage may have lasting connections to health.
paras.zh: 他们的重点是前 1000 天，从受孕到孩子两周岁左右。在此期间，器官发育，控制能量使用和激素反应的系统形成。此阶段的营养状况可能与健康有着持久的联系。

paras.en: Previous research using the same historical divide linked early rationing exposure to lower risks of diabetes and high blood pressure. The new team examined a biological age estimate reflecting the body's broader condition.
paras.zh: 先前的研究使用相同的历史鸿沟将早期配给暴露与较低的糖尿病和高血压风险联系起来。新团队检查了反映身体更广泛状况的生物年龄估计。

paras.en: They used blood measurements collected when participants were, on average, in their 50s. A method called PhenoAge combines chronological age with nine measurements, including blood sugar, inflammation markers, and blood cell characteristics.
paras.zh: 他们使用了参与者平均 50 多岁时收集的血液测量数据。一种称为 PhenoAge 的方法将实际年龄与九项测量值结合起来，包括血糖、炎症标记物和血细胞特征。

paras.en: PhenoAge estimates biological age using patterns associated with illness and mortality risk. Two people of the same chronological age can have different results. The team calculated how far each participant's estimated biological age departed from the value expected for someone their age.
paras.zh: PhenoAge 使用与疾病和死亡风险相关的模式来估计生物年龄。两个年龄相同的人可能会产生不同的结果。研究小组计算了每个参与者的估计生物年龄与同龄人的预期值的偏差有多大。

paras.en: After accounting for factors including age, sex, birthplace, and maternal smoking around birth, exposure before birth alone was associated with a biological age acceleration measure approximately 0.26 years lower than in unexposed participants. That represents a difference of roughly three months.
paras.zh: 在考虑了年龄、性别、出生地和母亲出生前后吸烟等因素后，仅出生前接触过的参与者的生物年龄加速测量值比未接触过的参与者低约 0.26 岁。这代表大约三个月的差异。

paras.en: When rationing also covered part of the first year after birth, the difference increased to around four and a half months, reaching roughly five months when exposure extended into the second year.
paras.zh: 当配给也覆盖出生后第一年的部分时间时，差异增加到大约四个半月，当暴露延伸到第二年时，差异达到大约五个月。

paras.en: The association appeared in both sexes, although it was stronger among women. A similar pattern persisted across groups with different genetic susceptibility to accelerated biological aging.
paras.zh: 这种关联在两性中都存在，但在女性中更为强烈。类似的模式在具有不同加速生物衰老遗传易感性的群体中持续存在。

paras.en: The team also examined 6,105 people born outside the UK during the same period. They found no comparable pattern linked to birth timing, although this smaller comparison group couldn't rule out broader changes over time.
paras.zh: 该团队还对同期出生在英国以外的 6,105 人进行了检查。他们没有发现与出生时间相关的可比较模式，尽管这个较小的比较组不能排除随着时间的推移发生更广泛的变化。

paras.en: The researchers then examined hospital records following participants' recruitment. Exposure before birth and into the first two years was associated with a 17 percent lower risk of age-related cataract, a clouding of the eye's lens, and a 22 percent lower risk of chronic kidney disease.
paras.zh: 研究人员随后检查了参与者招募后的医院记录。出生前和出生后两年内接触该物质可使患年龄相关性白内障、晶状体混浊的风险降低 17%，患慢性肾病的风险降低 22%。

paras.en: One possible explanation involves how the developing body responds to nutrition. Early conditions may influence blood sugar regulation, hormone responses, and organ development in ways that persist into adulthood.
paras.zh: 一种可能的解释涉及发育中的身体如何对营养做出反应。早期病症可能会影响血糖调节、激素反应和器官发育，并持续到成年。

paras.en: The study found differences in measurements including blood sugar and white blood cell counts. These findings don't establish the mechanism connecting early nutrition with adult health.
paras.zh: 该研究发现血糖和白细胞计数等测量值存在差异。这些发现并未建立早期营养与成人健康之间的联系机制。

paras.en: Nor does the five-month difference mean participants would live five months longer. Blood measurements captured one period, so they couldn't reveal how quickly individuals aged over time.
paras.zh: 五个月的差异也不意味着参与者会多活五个月。血液测量记录了一个时期的情况，因此无法揭示个体随着时间的推移衰老的速度。

paras.en: There were no clear associations with damage to the optic nerve known as glaucoma or with deterioration of central vision called age-related macular degeneration. Nor were there clear links with the bone-weakening condition osteoporosis or with dementia.
paras.zh: 与称为青光眼的视神经损伤或称为年龄相关性黄斑变性的中央视力恶化没有明显的关联。与骨质疏松症或痴呆症也没有明显的联系。

paras.en: Individual sugar consumption was unknown. Findings remained broadly consistent after accounting for food prices and other dietary changes, but other postwar changes couldn't be ruled out. Most participants were White, also limiting generalizability.
paras.zh: 个人糖消耗量未知。在考虑了食品价格和其他饮食变化后，研究结果基本保持一致，但不能排除其他战后变化。大多数参与者是白人，这也限制了普遍性。

paras.en: The study doesn't prove that reducing sugar early in life prevents disease. It offers clues for investigating how nutrition during pregnancy and infancy may connect to health decades later.
paras.zh: 该研究并没有证明在生命早期减少糖分可以预防疾病。它为调查怀孕和婴儿期间的营养如何与几十年后的健康联系提供了线索。

paras.en: The research has been published in Nature Communications.
paras.zh: 该研究已发表在《自然通讯》上。

articles.title: New Theory Explains Why The Right Side of The Brain Controls The Left Side of The Body
articles.author: David Nield

paras.en: The human brain, like the brains of most vertebrates, has a lot of crossed wiring in it.
paras.zh: 人类的大脑，就像大多数脊椎动物的大脑一样，里面有很多交叉的线路。

paras.en: The left part of our brains controls the right part of our bodies (and vice versa), while sensory inputs from our right side are processed in the left side of the brain (and vice versa).
paras.zh: 我们大脑的左侧部分控制身体的右侧部分（反之亦然），而来自右侧的感觉输入则在大脑的左侧进行处理（反之亦然）。

paras.en: Many different hypotheses have been put forward as to why this is the case, but the biological and evolutionary reasoning hasn't been satisfactorily settled yet.
paras.zh: 关于为什么会出现这种情况，人们提出了许多不同的假设，但生物学和进化推理尚未得到令人满意的解决。

paras.en: Now neuroscientists Martin Wessendorf and Daniel Wang, from the University of Minnesota, have published a study in Frontiers in Neuroanatomy in which they suggest a new explanation for this crossed (or contralateral) wiring.
paras.zh: 现在，明尼苏达大学的神经科学家 Martin Wessendorf 和 Daniel Wang 在《神经解剖学前沿》上发表了一项研究，其中他们对这种交叉（或对侧）接线提出了新的解释。

paras.en: Wessendorf and Wang take an evolutionary perspective, looking back through hundreds of millions of years for the first evidence of contralateral organization in animals.
paras.zh: 韦森多夫和王从进化的角度来看，回顾了数亿年，寻找动物对侧组织的第一个证据。

paras.en: "Many studies of lateralization have been published over the past 50 years," write the researchers in their published paper.
paras.zh: 研究人员在发表的论文中写道：“过去 50 年来，发表了许多关于偏侧化的研究。”

paras.en: "To date, though, there appears to have been no attempt to synthesize these studies into an evolutionary history of contralaterally organized brain circuits."
paras.zh: “然而，迄今为止，似乎还没有尝试将这些研究综合成对侧组织的大脑回路的进化史。”

paras.en: The researchers didn't carry out any new experiments or uncover any new fossils. Instead, they looked at existing studies on all the major vertebrate groups, from amphibians to mammals, to analyze how crossed pathways overlapped between species.
paras.zh: 研究人员没有进行任何新的实验或发现任何新的化石。相反，他们研究了对所有主要脊椎动物群体（从两栖动物到哺乳动物）的现有研究，以分析交叉路径如何在物种之间重叠。

paras.en: According to the researchers, the first wire crossing most likely happened in vision, and specifically in jawless fish over 500 million years ago.
paras.zh: 研究人员表示，第一次电线穿越很可能发生在视觉中，特别是在 5 亿多年前的无颌鱼类中。

paras.en: The eyes of these fish naturally flipped incoming light, and the signals from each eye crossed over to the opposite side of a part of the brain called the optic tectum (or the superior colliculus in mammals).
paras.zh: 这些鱼的眼睛自然地翻转入射光，并且来自每只眼睛的信号穿过大脑中称为视顶盖（或哺乳动物中的上丘）的部分的另一侧。

paras.en: Then, as sensory inputs for touch, vibration, and pain began to develop, they essentially followed the lead set by the optic tectum.
paras.zh: 然后，随着触摸、振动和疼痛的感觉输入开始发展，它们基本上遵循视顶盖的引导。

paras.en: By the time mammals came along with their more advanced cerebral cortex, the researchers argue, it made the most sense in terms of evolutionary efficiency to build on top of the existing contralateral arrangement rather than start again and switch all the wiring back again.
paras.zh: 研究人员认为，当哺乳动物出现更先进的大脑皮层时，从进化效率的角度来看，在现有的对侧排列之上进行构建是最有意义的，而不是重新开始并将所有线路重新切换回来。

paras.en: "We propose that the contralateral organization of the optic tectum biased the subsequent evolution of sensory and motor systems toward contralateral organization," write the researchers.
paras.zh: 研究人员写道：“我们认为，视顶盖的对侧组织使感觉和运动系统的后续进化偏向对侧组织。”

paras.en: "By the time true mammals appeared about 165 million years ago, their contralaterally organized somatosensory, rubrospinal, and tectospinal systems had already existed for almost 200 million years."
paras.zh: “当真正的哺乳动物在大约 1.65 亿年前出现时，它们的对侧组织的体感、红核脊髓和顶盖脊髓系统已经存在了近 2 亿年。”

paras.en: This is usually the path that evolution follows, for expediency – adapting what's already in place rather than inventing something completely new.
paras.zh: 这通常是进化所遵循的道路，为了权宜之计——适应已经存在的东西，而不是发明全新的东西。

paras.en: Previous explanations have argued that the crossed wiring in our brains came about because it's somehow more efficient, or because the body of an ancient ancestor of all vertebrates got twisted. However, these explanations don't take into account the full evolutionary picture, suggest Wessendorf and Wang.
paras.zh: 之前的解释认为，我们大脑中交叉线路的出现是因为它在某种程度上更有效率，或者是因为所有脊椎动物的远古祖先的身体都扭曲了。然而，韦森多夫和王认为，这些解释并没有考虑到完整的进化图景。

paras.en: That's not to say the matter is now settled. Future studies of ancient fossils, looking for further evidence of the theory, should tell us more about its credibility, in particular fossils of those 500-million-year-old fish.
paras.zh: 这并不是说事情现在已经解决了。未来对古代化石的研究，寻找该理论的进一步证据，应该告诉我们更多关于它的可信度，特别是那些 5 亿年前的鱼类化石。

paras.en: In addition, the theory could be put to the test by analyzing the neural wiring of animals that haven't been fully mapped yet, including crocodiles and birds. The differences and similarities found there would offer more clues about where contralateral organization appeared in evolutionary history.
paras.zh: 此外，还可以通过分析尚未完全绘制的动物（包括鳄鱼和鸟类）的神经线路来检验该理论。在那里发现的差异和相似之处将为了解对侧组织在进化史上的出现位置提供更多线索。

paras.en: Now the theory has been documented though – and traced back through millions of years – it can be prodded and probed, and the researchers behind it believe it'll hold up.
paras.zh: 现在，这个理论已经被记录下来——并且可以追溯到数百万年前——它可以被推动和探索，而且其背后的研究人员相信它会站得住脚。

paras.en: "As the neocortex evolved, the most economical way for it to integrate with those pathways was by being contralaterally organized, with the right side of the brain responsible for the left side of the body," write the researchers.
paras.zh: 研究人员写道：“随着新皮质的进化，它与这些通路整合的最经济的方式是通过对侧组织，让大脑的右侧负责身体的左侧。”

paras.en: "We predict that in most or all vertebrate brains, the existing contralaterally organized 'wiring design' will be found to be more efficient than any plausible ipsilaterally organized alternatives."
paras.zh: “我们预测，在大多数或所有脊椎动物的大脑中，现有的对侧组织的‘线路设计’将比任何可能的同侧组织的替代方案更有效。”

paras.en: The research has been published in Frontiers in Neuroanatomy.
paras.zh: 该研究已发表在《神经解剖学前沿》上。

articles.title: NASA's powerful Moon rocket engine roars through a dramatic 200-second test

paras.en: NASA's powerful Moon rocket engine roars through a dramatic 200-second test
paras.zh: NASA 强大的月球火箭发动机通过了 200 秒的戏剧性测试

paras.en: - NASA has successfully tested a powerful RS-25 rocket engine, firing it for 200 seconds to gather data that could make future Moon missions safer and more reliable. The test supports preparations for the 2028 Artemis IV Moon landing and NASAâs ultimate ambition of sending astronauts to Mars.
paras.zh: - NASA 已成功测试了强大的 RS-25 火箭发动机，点火 200 秒以收集数据，使未来的月球任务更加安全可靠。该测试支持 2028 年阿耳忒弥斯四号登月计划和 NASA 将宇航员送上火星的最终目标的准备工作。

paras.en: NASA has successfully completed another powerful rocket engine test as the agency prepares for future Artemis missions that will return astronauts to the Moon and lay the groundwork for human exploration of Mars.
paras.zh: 美国国家航空航天局 (NASA) 成功完成了另一项强大的火箭发动机测试，该机构正在为未来的阿耳忒弥斯任务做准备，该任务将使宇航员重返月球，并为人类探索火星奠定基础。

paras.en: On November 18, engineers fired RS-25 engine No. 10001 at the Fred Haise Test Stand at NASA's Stennis Space Center, located near Bay St. Louis, Mississippi. The developmental engine ran for its full scheduled duration of three minutes and 20 seconds (200 seconds).
paras.zh: 11 月 18 日，工程师们在位于密西西比州圣路易斯湾附近的 NASA 斯坦尼斯航天中心的 Fred Haise 试验台上点火了 10001 号 RS-25 发动机。开发引擎运行了 3 分 20 秒（200 秒）的完整预定持续时间。

paras.en: Although this particular engine is not intended for spaceflight, the successful test will provide NASA and its primary contractor, L3Harris Technologies, with valuable performance data. Engineers will use the results to improve the power, efficiency, and reliability of RS-25 engines designed for upcoming Artemis missions.
paras.zh: 尽管这款特殊发动机并非用于太空飞行，但成功的测试将为 NASA 及其主要承包商 L3Harris Technologies 提供有价值的性能数据。工程师将利用这些结果来提高为即将到来的阿尔忒弥斯任务设计的 RS-25 发动机的功率、效率和可靠性。

paras.en: Powerful RS-25 Engines Will Help Send Astronauts Back to the Moon
paras.zh: 强大的 RS-25 发动机将帮助宇航员重返月球

paras.en: NASA is preparing for Artemis IV, a mission scheduled for 2028 that aims to land astronauts on the lunar surface. The mission will launch from NASA's Kennedy Space Center in Florida, using the massive Space Launch System (SLS) rocket to carry astronauts aboard the Orion spacecraft.
paras.zh: NASA 正在为阿耳忒弥斯 IV 号任务做准备，这项任务计划于 2028 年进行，旨在将宇航员送上月球表面。该任务将从美国宇航局位于佛罗里达州的肯尼迪航天中心发射，使用大型太空发射系统（SLS）火箭将宇航员送上猎户座飞船。

paras.en: Artemis IV represents an important step toward NASA's larger ambitions. The agency plans to explore the Moon's South Pole, establish a sustained human presence on the lunar surface, and develop the experience and technologies needed for the first crewed journey to Mars.
paras.zh: 阿耳忒弥斯四号代表着美国宇航局朝着更大雄心壮志迈出的重要一步。该机构计划探索月球南极，在月球表面建立持续的人类存在，并开发首次载人火星之旅所需的经验和技术。

paras.en: The RS-25 engines play a crucial role in making these missions possible. Each SLS rocket uses four of the engines, which together generate up to 2 million pounds of thrust to help propel the spacecraft off the launchpad and into space.
paras.zh: RS-25 发动机在实现这些任务方面发挥着至关重要的作用。每枚 SLS 火箭均使用四个发动机，这些发动机共同产生高达 200 万磅的推力，帮助将航天器推离发射台并进入太空。

paras.en: Before any RS-25 engine is cleared for flight, it must undergo testing at NASA's Stennis Space Center to verify that it can perform reliably under the extreme conditions of a rocket launch.
paras.zh: 任何 RS-25 发动机在获准飞行之前，都必须在 NASA 斯坦尼斯航天中心接受测试，以验证其能够在火箭发射的极端条件下可靠地运行。

paras.en: These tests are carried out by specialists from NASA, L3Harris Technologies, and Nova Space Solutions, working together to ensure the engines are ready to power future journeys beyond Earth.
paras.zh: 这些测试由来自 NASA、L3Harris Technologies 和 Nova Space Solutions 的专家进行，他们共同努力确保发动机做好准备，为未来地球以外的旅程提供动力。

articles.title: A decades-old mystery about light could hold the key to faster internet

paras.en: A decades-old mystery about light could hold the key to faster internet
paras.zh: 关于光的数十年之谜可能是更快互联网的关键

paras.en: - A promising material for ultra-fast optical communications has held a secret for decades, but scientists may have finally cracked it. Researchers at KAIST and Caltech have precisely measured how barium titanate controls and absorbs light, resolving longstanding uncertainties that have slowed its development. Their findings could make it easier to build optical devices that transmit information faster while wasting less light.
paras.zh: - 一种用于超高速光通信的有前景的材料几十年来一直是个秘密，但科学家们可能最终破解了它。韩国科学技术院和加州理工学院的研究人员精确测量了钛酸钡如何控制和吸收光，解决了长期以来阻碍其发展的不确定性。他们的发现可以使制造光学设备变得更容易，这些设备可以更快地传输信息，同时浪费更少的光。

paras.en: Light can carry vast amounts of information, but developing faster and more efficient optical communication systems requires precise control over how it travels.
