You’ve probably already guessed that the singers she’s referring to aren’t human, but she’s not talking about birdsong, either. She’s talking about the indri, which is a very vocal—and very loud—species of lemur.
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：这是瓦莱里娅·费拉里奥（Valeria Ferrario），意大利都灵大学的博士后研究员。你可能已经猜到她所指的歌手不是人类，但她也不是在谈论鸟鸣。她说的是狐猴，这是一种叫声非常响亮的狐猴品种。

paras.en: Ferrario: It’s really loud. I would say it’s scary sometimes because maybe you’re following them, and they start singing, and it’s like, “Oh, my god.” But, but it’s really magical.
paras.zh: 费拉里奥：声音真的很大。我会说有时这很可怕，因为也许你在跟着他们，然后他们开始唱歌，就像，“哦，我的上帝。”但是，但是确实很神奇。

paras.en: Feltman: When most of us think about lemurs, we probably don’t imagine them singing. Apologies to those freaky little dudes from the Madagascar movies.
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：当我们大多数人想到狐猴时，我们可能不会想象它们会唱歌。向马达加斯加电影中那些怪异的小家伙道歉。

paras.en: [ CLIP: “I Like to Move It,” in Madagascar]
paras.zh: [剪辑：“我喜欢移动它”，马达加斯加]

paras.en: Feltman: In fairness, of the more than 100 estimated species of lemurs found on the aforementioned island, the Indri indri is the only true singer. That’s not to say that other lemurs can’t make lovely sounds, and in fact, I’m not sure I would die on the hill of saying that the indris are making particularly lovely sounds. But indris are the only lemurs that turn their vocalizations into what researchers feel comfortable calling songs. A song, in this case, is a long vocalization built from notes that are organized into phrases and follow a rhythm, with changes in pitch along the way. The question is why indris evolved to do this—and why other lemurs didn’t.
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：公平地说，在上述岛上发现的估计有 100 多种狐猴中，因德里狐猴是唯一真正的歌手。这并不是说其他​​狐猴不能发出可爱的声音，事实上，我不确定我会死在说狐猴发出特别可爱的声音上。但狐猴是唯一能将声音转化为研究人员认为的歌曲的狐猴。在这种情况下，歌曲是由音符组成的长发声，这些音符被组织成短语并遵循节奏，并且音高一路变化。问题是为什么狐猴进化到可以做到这一点，而其他狐猴却没有。

paras.en: Lemurs, by the way, have a fascinating evolutionary history. Like 90 percent of the living things on Madagascar, they aren’t found anywhere else. But based on the fossil record, it does not seem like lemurs evolved from a primate that was on Madagascar when it separated from Africa some 165 million years ago or when it broke away from India 80 million years ago and became an island. Instead, as wild as it might sound, lemur ancestors from Africa made their way to Madagascar by sea. According to DNA analysis published last year in Nature Communications, that happened about 53 million years ago.
paras.zh: 顺便说一句，狐猴有着令人着迷的进化历史。就像马达加斯加 90% 的生物一样，它们在其他地方找不到。但根据化石记录，狐猴似乎并不是由大约 1.65 亿年前马达加斯加岛脱离非洲或 8000 万年前脱离印度并成为岛屿时生活的灵长类动物进化而来。相反，尽管听起来很狂野，狐猴的祖先却从非洲经海路来到了马达加斯加。根据去年《自然通讯》杂志上发表的 DNA 分析，这发生在大约 5300 万年前。

paras.en: However it was that those little guys got swept onto shore, they found themselves without many natural predators or even any other primates to compete with. That’s probably why there are so many different species of lemur: There were lots of different niches for them to evolve into. And for the indri, one of those niches could be musicality. Besides humans and indris, the primates known to create songs are gibbons, tarsiers and titi monkeys—none of which are closely related to lemurs or to each other. That means this skill evolved more than once.
paras.zh: 然而，这些小家伙被冲上岸后，发现自己没有很多天敌，甚至没有任何其他灵长类动物可以与之竞争。这可能就是为什么有这么多不同种类的狐猴：有很多不同的生态位供它们进化。对于 indri 来说，这些利基之一可能是音乐性。除了人类和狐猴之外，已知会唱歌的灵长类动物还有长臂猿、眼镜猴和蒂蒂猴，它们与狐猴或彼此之间都没有密切关系。这意味着这项技能不止一次进化。

paras.en: Filippo Carugati: There is something in the ecology and the evolution that moved...the evolution of this peculiar kind of communication with musical communication in different primate species.
paras.zh: Filippo Carugati：生态学和进化中的某些东西推动了……不同灵长类动物中这种特殊的音乐交流方式的进化。

paras.en: Feltman: That’s Filippo Carugati, who worked on the University of Turin research on indris for his Ph.D. When I asked him what we know about why indris evolved to sing, he said that it’s still an open question—but that there are a few clues.
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：这是菲利波·卡鲁加蒂 (Filippo Carugati)，他在都灵大学攻读博士学位，从事 indris 的研究。当我问他我们对因德里斯为何进化成唱歌了解多少时，他说这仍然是一个悬而未决的问题，但有一些线索。

paras.en: Carugati: We need to look a bit to the function of the song itself. The songs is used for, uh, broadcasting, for, uh, signaling the occupation of a certain territory. So it is, is a way for signal to the neighboring groups, “Okay, we are this family of indris. We are occupying this territory. We are four individuals, two males, two females.” And they, and this is generally a very contagious behavior, so the neighboring groups are responding to this, saying, “Oh, in this territory we are five individuals, three males and two females,” and so on. And this is something that spread all over the forest.
paras.zh: 卡鲁加蒂：我们需要稍微了解一下歌曲本身的功能。这些歌曲是用来呃广播的,呃用来表示占领某个领土的。确实如此，这是向邻近群体发出信号的一种方式，“好吧，我们是这个因德里斯家族。我们正在占领这片领土。我们有四个人，两男两女。”他们，这通常是一种非常具有传染性的行为，所以邻近的群体对此做出反应，说，“哦，在这个领土上，我们有五个人，三男两女，”等等。而且这是遍布整个森林的东西。

paras.en: Feltman: Adult breeding pairs sing duets, and you can often tell which sex is which by the notes they use.
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：成年繁殖配对会唱二重唱，你通常可以通过它们使用的音符来辨别性别。

paras.en: It’s all very Rodgers and Hammerstein, if you ask me.
paras.zh: 如果你问我的话，这一切都非常罗杰斯和汉默斯坦。

paras.en: Filippo points out that this kind of family-to-family communication only works if your neighbors can hear you. That takes a lot of effort in the indris’ habitat, which is a rainforest full of hills and valleys.
paras.zh: 菲利波指出，这种家庭间的沟通只有在邻居能听到你说话的情况下才有效。在因德里斯的栖息地，这需要付出很大的努力，那里是一片充满丘陵和山谷的雨林。

paras.en: Carugati: So the important things is: the sound should be loud because the louder it is the more, uh, easily the other groups can, hear the occupation of the territory....And this is the main point, being heard and being loud.
paras.zh: 卡鲁加蒂：所以重要的是：声音应该响亮，因为声音越大，呃，其他群体就越容易听到占领领土的声音……这就是要点，被听到并且响亮。

paras.en: Feltman: Singing isn’t the only way to make your voice heard—lots of animals, including ones in similar environments, get loud without evolving the kind of rhythm and pitch these lemurs demonstrate. But according to Filippo, Valeria and their colleagues, indris use a trick to help their calls carry that’s inherently musical: they move their mouths kind of like opera singers do.

Carugati: Soprano singers or, or opera singers, uh, modify their mouth and especially, they adapt, the opening of the mouth with the higher notes. So the more, they open the mouth, the more the frequency of the notes emitted. We looked for this kind of relationship exact also in indri, and we found it.
paras.zh: 卡鲁加蒂：女高音歌手或歌剧歌手，呃，修改他们的嘴巴，特别是，他们适应高音时嘴巴的张开。因此，他们张开嘴的次数越多，发出音符的频率就越高。我们也在 indri 中寻找这种关系，并且我们找到了。

paras.en: Feltman: I decided to call someone who knows a lot more about opera singing than I do and who I can confirm—this is a compliment—is capable of being very, very loud.
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：我决定打电话给一个比我更了解歌剧演唱的人，我可以确认他（这是一种恭维）能够非常非常大声。

paras.en: Chelsea Feltman: As a singer, when you get, sort of, dialed into your support and your body, and you’re, like, producing sound really efficiently and just, like, naturally and freely, it does feel so animalistic.
paras.zh: 切尔西·费尔特曼：作为一名歌手，当你得到某种程度的支持和身体时，你会非常高效、自然、自由地发出声音，这确实让人感觉很兽性。

paras.en: Feltman: That’s my sister, Chelsea Feltman. She co-hosts a history and culture podcast called Vanity Veritas, and she trained as a soprano at the Juilliard School and the Mannes School of Music.
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：那是我的妹妹，切尔西·费尔特曼。她与人共同主持了一个名为“Vanity Veritas”的历史和文化播客，并在茱莉亚音乐学院和曼尼斯音乐学院接受了女高音培训。

paras.en: Chelsea: People think of opera singing as this very rarefied, cultured thing. But, like, I’m always telling people, like, it’s a, it’s like a bodily function when you’re doing it right.
paras.zh: 切尔西：人们认为歌剧演唱是一种非常高贵、有文化的东西。但是，就像，我总是告诉人们，就像，当你做得正确时，它就像一种身体机能。

paras.en: Feltman: I asked Chelsea to explain the singing technique these scientists are talking about.
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：我请切尔西解释一下这些科学家正在谈论的歌唱技巧。

paras.en: Chelsea: So basically, the vocal folds create the pitch, and that’s almost like plucking a string. The raw pitch comes from your vocal folds coming together and vibrating at a certain frequency, and then your vocal tract, which you can imagine as, like, your, your pharyngeal space, your throat, your mouth, is almost like the body of the instrument. So think about how, like, you pluck a guitar string, but the wooden body of the guitar is what makes it resonant.
paras.zh: 切尔西：基本上，声带产生音高，这几乎就像拨动一根弦一样。原始音高来自于你的声带聚集在一起并以一定的频率振动，然后你的声道，你可以想象成你的咽部空间，你的喉咙，你的嘴，几乎就像乐器的主体。所以想一下，就像你拨动吉他弦一样，但吉他的木质琴体才是让它产生共鸣的原因。

paras.en: Feltman: The vocal folds make the note, and the shape of the throat and mouth determines how it sounds. The technical term for the resonant frequencies in that space is formants. Opera singers learn to adjust their mouths so that the first formant lines up with the pitch they’re singing. That’s called formant tuning, which is what scientists think indris might be doing.
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：声带发出音符，喉咙和嘴巴的形状决定了它的发音。该空间中共振频率的技术术语是共振峰。歌剧歌手学习调整他们的嘴巴，使第一个共振峰与他们演唱的音高对齐。这就是所谓的共振峰调谐，科学家认为 indris 可能会这样做。

paras.en: Chelsea: As the pitch gets higher, the formant F1 has to get higher, and we do that by opening the mouth taller and taller.
paras.zh: 切尔西：随着音高变高，共振峰 F1 必须变高，我们通过将嘴巴张得越来越高来做到这一点。

paras.en: Feltman: This technique is especially useful for opera singers.
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：这种技术对于歌剧演员特别有用。

paras.en: Chelsea: As a classical soprano in this repertoire, we sing pitches that are way, way, way above the range of normal speech. So the fundamental is so high that we have to make the formant really, really high in order to get that resonance, which is why they’re talking about sopranos, in particular, opening up their mouth really—I’m, if you can’t see me, I’m opening up my mouth in, like, a very big “ah.”
paras.zh: 切尔西：作为这个曲目中的古典女高音，我们演唱的音高远远高于正常讲话的范围。所以基音太高了，我们必须让共振峰非常非常高才能获得共鸣，这就是为什么他们在谈论女高音，特别是张开嘴——我，如果你看不到我，我张开嘴，就像一个很大的“啊”。

paras.en: Feltman: To catch similar movement in indris, Filippo and his colleagues took a software called DeepLabCut, originally designed to track animal body movements in controlled situations—think lab mice being filmed in mazes—and trained it to find and measure points on a lemur’s face. Most of their footage turned out to be unusable because this was not a controlled situation. There were leaves, branches and lemurs swooping in at inconvenient angles. But they were able to track how mouth movement mapped to pitch change in a dozen individuals, and the pattern held: the higher the note, the more the mouth opened. The study can’t show that lemurs are doing this deliberately, of course, and it didn’t measure loudness directly. But it would make sense for formant tuning to help both species of singer out.
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：为了捕捉狐猴的类似运动，Filippo 和他的同事使用了一款名为 DeepLabCut 的软件，该软件最初设计用于在受控情况下跟踪动物的身体运动（想象一下在迷宫中拍摄的实验室老鼠），并训练它寻找和测量狐猴脸上的点。他们的大部分镜头最终无法使用，因为这不是一个受控的情况。树叶、树枝和狐猴以不方便的角度俯冲而下。但他们能够追踪十几个人的嘴巴运动如何映射到音高变化，并且该模式成立：音符越高，嘴巴张得越大。当然，这项研究不能表明狐猴是故意这样做的，而且它也没有直接测量响度。但通过共振峰调音来帮助这两种歌手摆脱困境是有意义的。

paras.en: Carugati: The ecological reason is clear because as soprano singers, indris need to be heard. So that’s, that’s the same evolutionary, we can say, pressure that [is] responsible for the, this convergent evolution of singing techniques in humans and in a species of lemurs that is separated from us 74 millions years ago.
paras.zh: 卡鲁加蒂：生态原因很明显，因为作为女高音歌手，因德里斯需要被听到。因此，我们可以说，这也是同样的进化压力，导致了人类和 7400 万年前与我们分离的狐猴物种歌唱技术的趋同进化。

paras.en: Feltman: You might not realize just how powerful a classically trained, aka operatic, voice can get—like, loud enough to fill concert halls without a microphone. Chelsea tells me that, among human singers, they don’t talk about this technique we’ve been going over making you louder, in terms of decibels, but more resonant. It’s that quality that makes lemur calls so piercing. That might not be a word I’d want to use to favorably describe a human singer, but the goal for an operatic soprano actually isn’t so far off.
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：你可能没有意识到，经过古典训练（又名歌剧）的声音可以变得多么强大——就像在没有麦克风的情况下大到足以充满音乐厅。切尔西告诉我，在人类歌手中，他们不会谈论我们一直在研究的这种让你声音更大（分贝）但更共鸣的技术。正是这种品质使得狐猴的叫声如此刺耳。我可能不想用这个词来形容人类歌手，但歌剧女高音的目标实际上并不遥远。

paras.en: Chelsea: If you ever feel like someone is onstage, but you hear their voice, like, ping you right in the ear, it’s like they’re right next to you, that’s formant frequencies. We talk about being able to cut through, having the ability to cut through an orchestra. ’Cause I’ll say the thing that’s special about opera singing is that we don’t use microphones. We don’t use amplification, which is why it’s so important to be able to do this and it’s kind of amazing that we can.
paras.zh: 切尔西：如果你感觉有人在舞台上，但你听到他们的声音，就像在你耳边叮叮当当，就好像他们就在你旁边，这就是共振峰频率。我们谈论能够突破，有能力突破管弦乐队。因为我想说歌剧演唱的特别之处在于我们不使用麦克风。我们不使用放大，这就是为什么能够做到这一点如此重要，而且我们能做到这一点真是令人惊奇。

paras.en: Feltman: That gets at the real commonality between human opera singers and indri lemurs: vocal efficiency. You might not realize it, but most of the qualities that make a voice sound “operatic” to the average person are about maximizing resonance.
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：这体现了人类歌剧歌手和狐猴之间真正的共同点：声音效率。您可能没有意识到，对于普通人来说，使声音听起来“歌剧”的大多数品质都是关于最大化共鸣。

paras.en: Chelsea: So opera prioritizes maximum efficiency of sound and resonance so that a voice can sustain these really high volumes and resonances and cut over an orchestra without amplification. Sometimes, when you hear an opera singer, everything just kinda sounds like…
paras.zh: 切尔西：所以歌剧优先考虑声音和共鸣的最大效率，以便声音能够维持这些非常高的音量和共鸣，并在不放大的情况下切换管弦乐队。有时候，当你听到歌剧歌手的声音时，一切听起来都像是……

paras.en: Chelsea: And you’re like, “I can’t understand what they’re saying.” Well, that is, that is because we have to modify vowels sort of well beyond or outside of how we would speak them because of this very idea of formant tuning. Like, if I want the note the pitch, to resonate optimally, I have to change the vowel because I have to adjust the vocal tract to tune the formant to the fundamentals. Other styles of music are able to maintain a more naturalistic, speechlike tone. Like, you think of your favorite pop singer who might sing in a way that feels very naturalistic. So those styles of music typically use, uh, microphones or amplification in order to have that more natural sound, naturalistic sound be, be heard in a large hall.
paras.zh: 切尔西：你会说，“我听不懂他们在说什么。”嗯，那是因为我们必须修改元音，使其远远超出我们所说的方式，因为共振峰调音的想法。就像，如果我想让音符的音高产生最佳共鸣，我必须改变元音，因为我必须调整声道以将共振峰调整到基本音。其他风格的音乐能够保持更自然、更像演讲的音调。就像，你想到你最喜欢的流行歌手可能会以一种非常自然的方式唱歌。因此，这些风格的音乐通常使用，呃，麦克风或扩音器，以便在大厅中听到更自然的声音，自然主义的声音。

paras.en: Feltman: It’s not just that opera singers don’t need microphones either. Microphones and opera singers really don’t get along.
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：不仅仅是歌剧演员不需要麦克风。麦克风和歌剧演员确实合不来。

paras.en: Chelsea: I have busted so many mics. They, they shut off. [Laughs] And I don’t even have a particularly big voice by operatic standards. Like, it’s just too much resonance and it’s, it sounds terrible. As opera singers, we have a specific set of skills that work really well for a very specific set of tasks
paras.zh: 切尔西：我弄坏了很多麦克风。他们，他们关闭了。 [笑]按照歌剧的标准，我什至没有特别大的声音。就像，它的共鸣太多了，而且听起来很糟糕。作为歌剧演员，我们拥有一套特定的技能，可以很好地完成一组非常特定的任务

paras.en: Feltman: As someone who’s been on the edges of the opera world since childhood, thanks to my sister, I’ve heard a lot of commentary on how dangerous it is to try to mimic the intensity of an operatic voice without actually using the techniques we’ve been talking about.
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：作为一个从小就处于歌剧世界边缘的人，多亏了我姐姐，我听到了很多评论，说在不实际使用我们一直在谈论的技术的情况下尝试模仿歌剧声音的强度是多么危险。

paras.en: Chelsea: This formant tuning helps us achieve this optimal resonance that’s really efficient, so we can have very full—I’ll use the word “piercing”—sounds without using a lot of pressure, without using a lot of muscular tension and blowing a lot of air through our vocal folds. Now, lots of people do that. Even really good singers can get into habits where they’re doing that and cause vocal injury. So it’s definitely very possible to chase that sound and not have the, the, the correct technique and really, really do yourself harm.
paras.zh: Chelsea：这种共振峰调音帮助我们实现真正高效的最佳共振，因此我们可以拥有非常饱满的声音（我将使用“刺耳”这个词），而无需使用很大的压力，不需要使用大量的肌肉张力，也不需要通过声带吹出大量的空气。现在，很多人都这样做。即使是非常优秀的歌手也会养成这样的习惯并导致声带受伤。因此，如果没有正确的技术去追逐那个声音，那么绝对有可能真的对自己造成伤害。

paras.en: Feltman: A lemur that blows out their voice faces higher stakes than a bad review, and they can’t make a career change. So while humans have developed countless, nuanced ways of singing—including many types of opera other than the western classical music we’ve been referring to today as opera for simplicity sake—it makes sense that these lemurs would most resemble the vocalists who prioritize being heard with minimal risk of injury. Of course, with all this in mind, I had to ask Chelsea what she thought of the lemurs’ technique.
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：一只放出声音的狐猴面临的风险比差评更高，而且它们无法改变职业。因此，虽然人类已经发展出了无数种微妙的歌唱方式——包括除西方古典音乐之外的许多类型的歌剧——为简单起见，我们今天将其称为歌剧——但这些狐猴最像那些优先考虑被听到且受伤风险最小的歌手，这是有道理的。当然，考虑到这一切，我不得不问切尔西她对狐猴技术的看法。

paras.en: Chelsea: Boy, are those lemurs talented. I think maybe it’s less surprising that animals or primates do it, and more surprising that, like, humans forgot how to do it, and somehow, like, worked their way back to it by, through this one weird form of singing that evolved in, in Europe in the early modern period.
paras.zh: 切尔西：天哪，那些狐猴很有天赋吗？我认为动物或灵长类动物这样做可能并不令人惊讶，更令人惊讶的是，比如，人类忘记了如何做到这一点，并且以某种方式，比如，通过这种在近代早期欧洲发展起来的奇怪的歌唱形式，又回到了原来的位置。

paras.en: Feltman: The Metropolitan Opera has had horses onstage before so maybe lemurs are next. I feel like Chelsea and I know a few composers who could probably make that happen.
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：大都会歌剧院以前曾在舞台上表演过马，所以也许狐猴是下一个。我觉得切尔西和我认识的一些作曲家可能会实现这一目标。

paras.en: Even if indris never make it to Lincoln Center, it seems like their singing technique helps them rise above the noise of the rainforest to communicate. And it turns out that their musicality could help the species survive in another way, too: Those distinct vocal characteristics could help scientists count them more easily. That’s important, because the species is listed as Critically Endangered by the International Union for Conservation of Nature, or IUCN, due to habitat destruction, hunting and climate change. In fact, researchers aren’t even sure how many of them are left.
paras.zh: 即使因德里斯从未到达林肯中心，他们的歌唱技巧似乎也能帮助他们超越雨林的噪音进行交流。事实证明，它们的音乐性也可以帮助该物种以另一种方式生存：这些独特的声音特征可以帮助科学家更容易地计算它们。这很重要，因为由于栖息地破坏、狩猎和气候变化，该物种被国际自然保护联盟（IUCN）列为极度濒危物种。事实上，研究人员甚至不确定还剩下多少。

paras.en: Ferrario: No one was able to, uh, grow this species in captivity, so they die in captivity.
paras.zh: Ferrario：没有人能够，呃，圈养这个物种，所以它们在圈养中死去。

paras.en: So the only place where we can work on their conservation is in, in nature. So basically, uh, the IUCN is asking for more data about the number and the abundance of the species in Madagascar.
paras.zh: 因此，我们唯一可以保护它们的地方就是大自然。所以基本上，呃，世界自然保护联盟正在要求提供有关马达加斯加物种数量和丰度的更多数据。

paras.en: Feltman: That was Valeria Ferrario again. She says lemurs are typically tough to count in person because they tend to avoid humans. Folks have had better luck than average at the protected wildlife park Maromizaha, which is where University of Turin researchers go to study indris because animals there are more accustomed to human presence. With a reasonably confident tally of lemurs to reference, Valeria and her colleagues decided to use Maromizaha as a proving ground for a new surveying method.
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：又是瓦莱里娅·费拉里奥。她说狐猴通常很难亲自数数，因为它们倾向于避开人类。在受保护的马罗米扎哈野生动物公园，人们的运气比平均水平要好，都灵大学的研究人员在那里研究因德里斯，因为那里的动物更习惯人类的存在。有了相当可靠的狐猴统计数据可供参考，瓦莱里娅和她的同事决定使用马罗米扎哈作为新测量方法的试验场。

paras.en: Drawing inspiration from previous work on beaked whales, they set out to use passive acoustic monitoring to record the singing lemurs.
paras.zh: 从之前对喙鲸的研究中汲取灵感，他们开始使用被动声学监测来记录狐猴的歌声。

paras.en: Ferrario: The initial idea we got inspired by, by a colleague of ours, uh, was really good, is from St. Andrews University [the University of St. Andrews in Scotland], and they created this method underwater. So uh, you can understand how the sound propagation is really different underwater, so it was kind of a, you know, a bet here because we didn’t know whether this method could work also on terrestrial and also in a really complex environment with, um, concern to sound, you know, because the forest is really, uh, loud, is really complex, and we have a lot of sounds, and it’s really difficult to measure how the sound propagates there with all the trees and the rain, and the wind and stuff like that...It’s a lot of statistics and so [laughs] it was quite complicated to do the same thing on the land.
paras.zh: Ferrario：我们最初的想法是受到我们的一位同事的启发，嗯，非常好，来自圣安德鲁斯大学（苏格兰圣安德鲁斯大学），他们在水下创造了这种方法。所以呃，你可以理解声音在水下的传播是如何不同的，所以这是一个，你知道，这里的一个赌注，因为我们不知道这种方法是否也适用于陆地，以及在一个非常复杂的环境中，嗯，关注声音，你知道，因为森林真的，呃，吵闹，非常复杂，而且我们有很多声音，很难测量声音如何在所有树木、雨水、风和诸如此类的东西中传播。那……有很多统计数据，所以[笑]在陆地上做同样的事情是相当复杂的。

paras.en: Feltman: Like, really complicated. First, recorders placed around the forest capture the entire soundscape—easy-peasy. Then a neural network picks out indri songs from the rest of the hustle and bustle because the rainforest is noisy. But then you get into the complicated statistics of it all because a recorder is only going to capture an unknown fraction of the songs getting sung in the survey area. The key to turning passive monitoring into a reliable head count is to calculate the probability that if a song happens, you’re going to hear it, because that allows you to take your indri mixtape and extrapolate how many songs happened during that time in total. That was especially tricky in Maromizaha.
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：确实很复杂。首先，放置在森林周围的录音机轻松捕捉整个音景。然后，神经网络从喧嚣的其他地方挑选出 indri 歌曲，因为雨林很吵。但随后您就会陷入复杂的统计数据中，因为录音机只能捕获调查区域中演唱的歌曲的未知部分。将被动监控转变为可靠的人数统计的关键是计算如果发生一首歌，你会听到它的概率，因为这可以让你利用你的 indri mixtape 并推断出在那段时间总共发生了多少首歌。这在 Maromizaha 中尤其棘手。

paras.en: Ferrario: Traditionally what happens is that you have a microphone, and you, uh, reproduce, like, from speakers, uh, the, the sound of your interest at different distances, and you try to understand how the sound propagates, you know, into the environment. But the difficult part of this in a tropical forest like Maromiza, is that there, uh, the environment is really complex. It’s just hills and stuff and valleys, so the sound travels in different ways. So this was the biggest complication for our study.
paras.zh: Ferrario：传统上，你有一个麦克风，然后你，呃，从扬声器，呃，在不同距离再现你感兴趣的声音，然后你尝试了解声音如何传播到环境中。但在像马罗米扎这样的热带森林里，困难之处在于，呃，环境真的很复杂。这里只是山丘、东西和山谷，所以声音以不同的方式传播。所以这是我们研究中最大的并发症。

paras.en: Feltman: Then you take everything you know about how often any given group of indris tends to sing.
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：然后你就可以了解任何特定群体唱歌的频率。

paras.en: Ferrario: You can compose all these things together and try to translate the number of songs into the number of groups basically.
paras.zh: Ferrario：你可以将所有这些东西组合在一起，并尝试将歌曲的数量基本上转化为组的数量。

paras.en: Feltman: When they compared the method’s estimate with the number of groups researchers already knew lived in the area, the two landed within about 10 percent of each other: roughly 5.5 groups per square kilometer versus 6.2. The margin of error around that estimate is wide, and this was just one site, so it’s still just a proof of concept. But Valeria is excited to see other groups try it.
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：当他们将该方法的估计值与研究人员已知居住在该地区的群体数量进行比较时，两者的差距约为 10%：每平方公里大约有 5.5 个群体，而每平方公里有 6.2 个群体。这一估计的误差范围很大，而且这只是一个站点，所以它仍然只是一个概念证明。但瓦莱里娅很高兴看到其他团体尝试这样做。

paras.en: Ferrario: It’s really, um, simple in some way. It was not simple to do this paper, but it’s something that is really, uh, democratic, I think. It’s really easy to, like, uh, learn it and how to use the microphones and how to use this information to gather information on biodiversity or a species, or so on. And that’s what I like the most because I think it’s really easy, like, to pass it to, uh, local researchers, even if they have no funding or stuff like that. So it’s really nice because I think this is the basis to build something sustainable in conservation, you know? If the conservation is really only linked to, uh, Italian people going there and living there and having the funding to do stuff there is one thing, but it could be sustainable only if local people and people living there can do this and, like, use this methodology there.
paras.zh: Ferrario：从某种程度上来说，这真的很简单。写这篇论文并不简单，但我认为这确实是，呃，民主的事情。这真的很容易，例如，呃，学习它以及如何使用麦克风以及如何使用这些信息来收集有关生物多样性或物种等的信息。这就是我最喜欢的，因为我认为将它传递给呃，当地研究人员真的很容易，即使他们没有资金或类似的东西。所以这真的很好，因为我认为这是建立可持续保护的基础，你知道吗？如果保护真的只与，呃，意大利人去那里生活，并有资金去做事情，那是一回事，但只有当地人和居住在那里的人们能够做到这一点，并且在那里使用这种方法，它才可能是可持续的。

paras.en: Feltman: So after millions of years of evolution turned indris into showstopping singers, scientists are tuning in with conservation in mind. The indris’ song could be the thing that helps save them.
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：经过数百万年的进化，因德里斯变成了令人惊叹的歌手，科学家们正在考虑保护环境。因德里斯人的歌声可能是拯救他们的力量。

paras.en: Feltman: That’s all for today’s episode. We’ll be back on Monday for our weekly science news roundup.
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：这就是今天这一集的全部内容。我们将于周一回来参加每周科学新闻综述。

paras.en: For Scientific American, this is Rachel Feltman. Have a great weekend!
paras.zh: 《科学美国人》的这位人物是雷切尔·费尔特曼 (Rachel Feltman)。周末愉快！

articles.title: What helps land recover after fire? This ecologist looks to the past
articles.author: Anna Mattson

paras.en: In an increasingly fire-prone western North America, Jennifer Grenz, an ecologist and member of the Lytton First Nation, looks at fire with a holistic eye. She considers her work with landscapes recovering from catastrophic wildfire to be “deliberately unfocused,” spanning soil microbial ecology, restoration ecology, invasion biology and historical biology.
paras.zh: 在越来越容易发生火灾的北美西部，生态学家兼利顿原住民成员詹妮弗·格伦茨 (Jennifer Grenz) 以整体的眼光看待火灾。她认为她对从灾难性野火中恢复的景观的研究“故意没有重点”，涵盖土壤微生物生态学、恢复生态学、入侵生物学和历史生物学。

paras.en: Grenz analyzes historical ecological records, like how Indigenous people have shaped and cared for ecosystems over time, to paint a comprehensive picture. “I’m interested in how those histories leave ecological legacies and hints of the stewardship of the past,” says Grenz, who leads the Indigenous Ecology Lab at the University of British Columbia in Canada. “What changed on the land that made it more vulnerable?”
paras.zh: 格伦茨分析了历史生态记录，例如土著人民如何随着时间的推移塑造和照顾生态系统，以描绘出一幅全面的图景。 “我对这些历史如何留下生态遗产和过去管理的暗示感兴趣，”加拿大不列颠哥伦比亚大学土著生态实验室的负责人格伦茨说。 “这片土地发生了什么变化，使其变得更加脆弱？”

paras.en: Grenz spends time with many kinds of specialists, such as archaeologists, anthropologists and Indigenous elders who provide oral histories.
paras.zh: 格伦茨与许多类型的专家共度时光，例如考古学家、人类学家和提供口述历史的土著长者。

paras.en: Moving forward, her lab will examine ecology below ground, including soil, microbial communities and root networks. The goal is to understand the role of underground ecology in critical topics like carbon sequestration, climate change, biodiversity and sustainable management.
paras.zh: 展望未来，她的实验室将研究地下生态，包括土壤、微生物群落和根系网络。目标是了解地下生态在碳封存、气候变化、生物多样性和可持续管理等关键主题中的作用。

paras.en: “My motivation is in our interior Salish Territories in the southern interior of British Columbia, where my ancestors rest and where my people are,” Grenz says. “The responsibility I feel to them and to our Tmícw, which means our lands, [is] to not take us back to the past, but to show that we have the deep knowledge to help us move forward.”
paras.zh: “我的动机是在不列颠哥伦比亚省南部内陆的萨利什​​领地，那里是我的祖先安息的地方，也是我的人民居住的地方，”格伦茨说。 “我对他们和我们的 Tmícw（这意味着我们的土地）感到的责任是不要让我们回到过去，而是要表明我们拥有深厚的知识来帮助我们前进。”

articles.title: This scientist proves which problems computers can’t solve quickly
articles.author: Anna Mattson

paras.en: Dor Minzer remembers sitting in an undergraduate computation class at Tel Aviv University. He was intrigued by his professor and soon found himself pulled into a new world: the mystifying intersection of math and computation, first laid out by Alan Turing during World War II. Working with the professor, Minzer became deeply interested in the limitations of what computers can and can’t do.
paras.zh: 多尔·明泽 (Dor Minzer) 记得参加特拉维夫大学的本科生计算课。他对教授很感兴趣，很快就发现自己被带入了一个新世界：数学与计算的神秘交叉点，这是阿兰·图灵在二战期间首次提出的。与教授一起工作，明泽对计算机能做什么和不能做什么的局限性产生了浓厚的兴趣。

paras.en: “My part is actually to prove not only do I not know how to do it, but I can prove that it’s impossible,” Minzer says. “You have to really be curious.”
paras.zh: “我的职责实际上是证明我不仅不知道如何做到这一点，而且我可以证明这是不可能的，”明泽说。 “你必须真正感到好奇。”

paras.en: Minzer’s hard work has paid off. In 2018, he proved a theoretical computer science problem called the 2-to-2 games conjecture. It asks whether computers can efficiently distinguish games where almost all rules can be satisfied from those where almost none can be satisfied, when the rules have a strict structure.
paras.zh: 明泽的努力得到了回报。 2018年，他证明了一个名为“2对2博弈猜想”的计算机科学理论问题。它询问当规则具有严格的结构时，计算机是否能够有效区分几乎所有规则都可以满足的游戏和几乎没有规则可以满足的游戏。

paras.en: In September, Minzer and his two graduate students at MIT posted a 95-page milestone paper on the unique games conjecture, which builds off the 2-to-2 conjecture. The paper wasn’t quite ready, but they published to get ahead of a press release from OpenAI, describing its proof for the same problem, slated for only days later. It’s a situation that many mathematicians have found themselves in this year as AI companies flood the field with findings at lightning speed.
paras.zh: 9 月份，明泽和他在麻省理工学院的两名研究生发表了一篇长达 95 页的里程碑式论文，内容涉及独特的游戏猜想，该猜想建立在 2-2 猜想的基础上。这篇论文还没有完全准备好，但他们在 OpenAI 发布新闻稿之前发表，描述了同一问题的证明，该新闻稿定于几天后发布。今年，随着人工智能公司以闪电般的速度将研究成果涌入该领域，许多数学家都遇到了这种情况。

paras.en: Minzer says it’s critical to remember that math, and all the research and contemplation behind it, is very human. “It’s a human activity,” he says. “Research is sort of a living organism, a living body.”
paras.zh: 明泽说，重要的是要记住，数学及其背后的所有研究和思考都是非常人性化的。 “这是一项人类活动，”他说。 “研究是一个活的有机体，一个活的身体。”

paras.en: Minzer teaches his own students now. Some days, he talks to his class and gets the sense that nobody is paying attention. But other days, he gets a few students that participate. They have ideas, they’re excited, and they remind him of his own days as a graduate student.
paras.zh: 明泽现在教自己的学生。有时，他在班上讲话时，会感觉到没有人注意。但其他时候，他也会有一些学生参加。他们有想法，他们很兴奋，他们让他想起自己作为研究生的日子。

paras.en: “I feel like now I feel like I’m passing the torch,” he says. “Before you have a Ph.D. adviser, you’re like a new person in a dark room. There are infinite places to go. Your Ph.D. adviser is the person that holds your hand and says, ‘Okay, let’s walk here.’”
paras.zh: “我觉得现在我正在传递火炬，”他说。 “在没有博士生导师之前，你就像一个黑屋子里的新人。有无数个地方可以去。你的博士生导师就是那个握着你的手说：‘好吧，我们走到这里’的人。”

articles.title: Astronomer Isabel Angelo hunts for odd signals in telescope data
articles.author: Anna Mattson

paras.en: Isabel Angelo spends her days searching the cosmos for exoplanets and signs of extraterrestrial intelligence. But Angelo’s head isn’t in the stars. It’s buried under mountains of 0s and 1s — data from space telescopes old and new.
paras.zh: 伊莎贝尔·安吉洛（Isabel Angelo）整天在宇宙中寻找系外行星和外星智慧生物的迹象。但安吉洛的头脑并不在星星上。它被埋在堆积如山的 0 和 1 之下——来自新旧太空望远镜的数据。

paras.en: To piece together a fuller picture of what’s out there (alien megastructures around nearby stars, perhaps?), Angelo and her colleagues at the SETI Institute in Mountain View, Calif., are turning to machine learning models. These tools are analyzing the troves of telescope data for anomalies — things that look “weird” in space that we don’t know how to explain yet.
paras.zh: 为了更全面地了解那里的情况（也许是附近恒星周围的外星巨型结构？），安吉洛和她在加利福尼亚州山景城 SETI 研究所的同事们正在转向机器学习模型。这些工具正在分析大量望远镜数据中的异常现象——那些在太空中看起来“奇怪”但我们还不知道如何解释的东西。

paras.en: Most of the space weirdos will probably turn out to be total normies — a comet, a newborn star or a star surrounded by lots of gas and dust. “These are things that I would expect [the models] to find,” Angelo says. “But the goal is to find something that’s not even in any of these categories.”
paras.zh: 大多数太空怪人可能最终都是完全正常的——一颗彗星、一颗新生恒星或一颗被大量气体和尘埃包围的恒星。 “这些是我期望[模型]找到的东西，”安吉洛说。 “但我们的目标是找到一些不属于这些类别的东西。”

paras.en: In the meantime, Angelo keeps her whimsy and wonder for space alive by remembering historic moments, like the reveal of the first portrait of a black hole in 2019. The scientists “put all of these telescopes all over the Earth. They wait for the Earth to rotate. They do all this math to construct this one image,” Angelo says. “I can’t believe how creative and innovative we have to be to learn about space. It’s such a specific and really fun challenge.”
paras.zh: 与此同时，安杰洛通过记住历史时刻，比如 2019 年第一张黑洞肖像的揭晓，来保持她对太空的奇思妙想和好奇心。科学家们“将所有这些望远镜放在地球各地。他们等待地球自转。他们进行所有这些数学计算来构建这幅图像，”安杰洛说。 “我不敢相信我们需要多么有创意和创新才能了解太空。这是一个非常具体且非常有趣的挑战。”

articles.title: Screen Time in Childhood Is Linked to a Surprising Brain Benefit in Teens, 8-Year Study Finds
articles.author: Peter Dockrill

paras.en: For young families, screens are equal parts blessing and curse.
paras.zh: 对于年轻家庭来说，屏幕既是福也是祸。

paras.en: Tablets, phones, computers, and TVs easily keep children entertained and occupied, but research suggests screens may lead to troubling behaviors in children, potentially stunting their development, and posing a number of health issues as they get older.
paras.zh: 平板电脑、手机、电脑和电视很容易让孩子们娱乐和忙碌，但研究表明，屏幕可能会导致儿童出现令人不安的行为，可能阻碍他们的发育，并随着年龄的增长带来许多健康问题。

paras.en: Insufficient levels of physical activity are also linked to poorer cognition in children, so it's conceivable that if screen time takes away from their exercise, it might affect their cognitive abilities, not just their physical development.
paras.zh: 体力活动不足也与儿童认知能力较差有关，因此可以想象，如果屏幕时间减少了他们的锻炼时间，可能会影响他们的认知能力，而不仅仅是身体发育。

paras.en: (Although, if you've ever tried to take an iPad off a toddler, you've likely observed their profound physical strength.)
paras.zh: （不过，如果您曾经尝试过从幼儿身上拿走 iPad，您可能已经观察到了他们强大的体力。）

paras.en: While previous research has explored the links between children's physical activity, screen time, and cognition, we still don't know much about how these behaviors accumulate throughout childhood and relate to cognitive performance in adolescence.
paras.zh: 虽然之前的研究已经探索了儿童的身体活动、屏幕时间和认知之间的联系，但我们仍然不太清楚这些行为是如何在整个童年时期积累的，以及与青春期认知表现的关系。

paras.en: In a new study in Pediatric Exercise Science, researchers sought to address the gap – and the results might come as a bit of a surprise.
paras.zh: 在儿科运动科学的一项新研究中，研究人员试图弥补这一差距，结果可能会有点令人惊讶。

paras.en: In the study, researchers analyzed eight years of data collected from 260 children (136 boys and 124 girls) who took part in a larger research project called the Finnish PANIC study, which began when the children were about eight years old, with follow-ups ending when they were approximately 16.
paras.zh: 在这项研究中，研究人员分析了从 260 名儿童（136 名男孩和 124 名女孩）收集的 8 年数据，这些儿童参加了一项名为芬兰 PANIC 研究的大型研究项目，该研究在孩子们大约 8 岁的时候开始，随访在孩子们大约 16 岁的时候结束。

paras.en: As part of the PANIC study, researchers recorded the children's levels of physical activity, sedentary time, and screen time, sourced from questionnaires during the study and using data from wearable activity trackers worn by the participants.
paras.zh: 作为 PANIC 研究的一部分，研究人员记录了孩子们的体力活动水平、久坐时间和屏幕时间，这些数据来自研究期间的问卷调查，并使用参与者佩戴的可穿戴活动追踪器的数据。

paras.en: In addition, at the final follow-up session, the participants did a series of tests to assess their cognitive function, including memory, attention, reaction time, and other factors.
paras.zh: 此外，在最后的后续会议中，参与者进行了一系列测试来评估他们的认知功能，包括记忆力、注意力、反应时间和其他因素。

paras.en: The results showed that children who reported more cumulative screen time during the study tended to perform better on the cognitive tests as adolescents, with higher overall cognition scores and faster reaction times on two working memory tasks.
paras.zh: 结果显示，在研究期间累计屏幕时间较多的儿童往往在青少年时期的认知测试中表现更好，总体认知得分较高，并且在两项工作记忆任务上的反应时间更快。

paras.en: "We should not regard screen time solely as harmful," says exercise researcher Petri Jalanko from the University of Jyväskylä in Finland.
paras.zh: 芬兰于韦斯屈莱大学的运动研究员佩特里·贾兰科 (Petri Jalanko) 表示：“我们不应该仅仅将屏幕时间视为有害。”

paras.en: "The findings suggest that screen time can support children's and adolescents' cognitive processing. Presumably, the essential point here is what kind of things they do in their screen time."
paras.zh: “研究结果表明，屏幕时间可以支持儿童和青少年的认知处理。大概，这里的要点是他们在屏幕时间做了什么样的事情。”

paras.en: Previous research has suggested that how screens are used matters more than just time overall spent engaging with devices, and we know that some forms of screen time, like playing video games, appear to confer benefits to children.
paras.zh: 之前的研究表明，屏幕的使用方式比使用设备所花费的总时间更重要，而且我们知道，某些形式的屏幕时间（例如玩视频游戏）似乎对儿童有好处。

paras.en: Similarly, the researchers here suggest that some screen time may include activities that improve cognition, such as playing video games, while other sedentary activities, like reading, writing, and doing homework, may also be beneficial.
paras.zh: 同样，研究人员建议，一些屏幕时间可能包括提高认知的活动，例如玩视频游戏，而其他久坐的活动，例如阅读、写作和做作业，也可能是有益的。

paras.en: In contrast, the familiar parental refrain of 'go outside and get some exercise' might not be quite as wise as we like to assume.
paras.zh: 相比之下，父母常说的“出去锻炼一下”可能并不像我们想象的那么明智。

paras.en: In the study, the researchers found a tentative association, especially among boys, that unsupervised physical activity was linked to lower performance in one of the cognitive memory tests.
paras.zh: 在这项研究中，研究人员发现了一种初步关联，特别是在男孩中，无人监督的体力活动与一项认知记忆测试中的较低表现有关。

paras.en: While the link across the whole group was not significant after further statistical analysis (though it held among boys), it could be a hint that unstructured physical activity can take time away from other activities that might enhance cognition, such as reading, writing, and doing homework.
paras.zh: 虽然在进一步的统计分析后，整个群体之间的联系并不显着（尽管在男孩中也存在这种联系），但这可能暗示，非结构化的身体活动可能会占用其他可能增强认知的活动的时间，例如阅读、写作和做作业。

paras.en: And even perhaps, ironically enough, some good old-fashioned screen time.
paras.zh: 讽刺的是，甚至可能还有一些不错的老式放映时间。

paras.en: The findings are reported in Pediatric Exercise Science.
paras.zh: 研究结果发表在《儿科运动科学》杂志上。

articles.title: A 3-Year-Old's Metastatic Cancer Vanished After Two Doses of Experimental Therapy
articles.author: Peter Dockrill

paras.en: A promising breakthrough in cancer treatment has given a young boy a new chance at life.
paras.zh: 癌症治疗的一项有希望的突破给了一个小男孩一个新的生命机会。

paras.en: Chimeric Antigen Receptor (CAR) T cell therapy is an immunotherapy technique that involves taking a patient's immune cells and genetically engineering them to become potent cancer-hunting predators.
paras.zh: 嵌合抗原受体 (CAR) T 细胞疗法是一种免疫疗法技术，涉及提取患者的免疫细胞并对它们进行基因改造，使其成为有效的癌症捕食者。

paras.en: The treatment has shown huge promise in helping patients treat cancer, although its effectiveness has mostly been limited to treating blood cancers, not solid tumors.
paras.zh: 这种疗法在帮助患者治疗癌症方面显示出巨大的前景，尽管其有效性主要限于治疗血癌，而不是实体瘤。

paras.en: But an inspirational real-life success story involving a three-year-old patient shows scientists are making big progress with CAR T cell therapy against solid tumors too – and with potentially life-saving results.
paras.zh: 但现实生活中一个涉及一名三岁患者的鼓舞人心的成功故事表明，科学家们在针对实体瘤的 CAR T 细胞疗法方面也取得了重大进展，并且可能会挽救生命。

paras.en: In a report published in The New England Journal of Medicine, researchers document a case of complete regression of hepatoblastoma, a form of malignant liver cancer, in a 3-year-old boy, after CAR T cell treatment.
paras.zh: 在《新英格兰医学杂志》发表的一份报告中，研究人员记录了一名 3 岁男孩在 CAR T 细胞治疗后肝母细胞瘤（一种恶性肝癌）完全消退的病例。

paras.en: "This case demonstrates that a durable complete response in a chemotherapy-resistant solid tumor can be achieved entirely in the outpatient setting without systemic toxicity," says first author and pediatric oncologist David Steffin from the Baylor College of Medicine in Houston, Texas.
paras.zh: “这个病例表明，化疗耐药实体瘤的持久完全缓解完全可以在门诊环境中实现，而不会产生全身毒性，”第一作者、德克萨斯州休斯顿贝勒医学院的儿科肿瘤学家 David Steffin 说。

paras.en: When the boy was first diagnosed, he had a mass in the left lobe of his liver that measured 11.2 cm by 9.6 cm by 7.1 cm (4.4 × 3.8 × 2.8 inches).
paras.zh: 当男孩第一次被诊断时，他的肝脏左叶有一个肿块，尺寸为 11.2 厘米 x 9.6 厘米 x 7.1 厘米（4.4 × 3.8 × 2.8 英寸）。

paras.en: The cancer had metastasized to his lungs, with indications that it had also spread to his bones.
paras.zh: 癌症已经转移到他的肺部，有迹象表明它也已经扩散到他的骨头。

paras.en: The boy received three bouts of chemotherapy and had his primary liver tumor surgically removed, along with two operations to remove the cancer that had spread to his lungs.
paras.zh: 该男孩接受了三轮化疗，并通过手术切除了原发性肝脏肿瘤，并进行了两次手术以切除已扩散到肺部的癌症。

paras.en: Despite the interventions, the cancer rapidly returned, with a new tumor appearing in his lungs.
paras.zh: 尽管采取了干预措施，癌症还是迅速复发，肺部出现了新的肿瘤。

paras.en: After the rapid recurrence, the boy was enrolled in the CARE study, the first human trial of an experimental form of CAR T cell therapy.
paras.zh: 病情迅速复发后，男孩参加了 CARE 研究，这是 CAR T 细胞疗法实验形式的首次人体试验。

paras.en: The boy received two infusions of the experimental GPC3-CAR treatment, made from his own T cells, but engineered to recognize glypican-3 (GPC3), a protein that is highly expressed in liver cancers.
paras.zh: 该男孩接受了两次实验性 GPC3-CAR 治疗的输注，该治疗由他自己的 T 细胞制成，但经过改造可以识别磷脂酰肌醇蛋白聚糖 3 (GPC3)，这是一种在肝癌中高度表达的蛋白质。

paras.en: The researchers also engineered the therapy to include genes that would express the immune proteins interleukin–15 and interleukin–21, to boost the CAR T cells' longevity and tumor-killing ability, based on previous evidence from preclinical models.
paras.zh: 研究人员还根据先前临床前模型的证据，设计了该疗法，使其包含表达免疫蛋白白细胞介素 15 和白细胞介素 21 的基因，以提高 CAR T 细胞的寿命和杀伤肿瘤的能力。

paras.en: After the first infusion, the patient showed a partial response, indicated by CT scans and falling levels of a protein called alpha-fetoprotein in his blood, which is indicative of tumor activity.
paras.zh: 第一次输注后，患者表现出部分反应，CT 扫描和血液中一种称为甲胎蛋白的蛋白质水平下降表明该患者表现出部分反应，该蛋白质是肿瘤活动的指标。

paras.en: Eight weeks later he received a second dose of the therapy, and follow-up scans showed no remaining signs of the disease, apart from some residual scarring.
paras.zh: 八周后，他接受了第二剂治疗，后续扫描显示，除了一些残留的疤痕外，没有任何剩余的疾病迹象。

paras.en: After 12 months, the boy was still disease-free – an incredible result and turnaround for the patient and his family, given the severity of his illness before his participation in the trial.
paras.zh: 12 个月后，男孩仍然没有患病——考虑到他在参加试验之前病情的严重程度，这对患者及其家人来说是一个令人难以置信的结果和转变。

paras.en: "This study provides evidence that these novel CAR T cells may be a safe and effective modality for hepatoblastoma and highlights the need for further assessment in patients with GPC3+ solid tumors," says co-author and pediatric oncologist Andras Heczey from Seattle Children's Hospital and the University of Washington.
paras.zh: “这项研究提供的证据表明，这些新型 CAR T 细胞可能是一种安全有效的肝母细胞瘤治疗方法，并强调了对 GPC3+ 实体瘤患者进行进一步评估的必要性，”西雅图儿童医院和华盛顿大学的合著者兼儿科肿瘤学家 Andras Heczey 说。

paras.en: As the researchers note, liver cancer is the third leading cause of cancer-related death globally, so making progress in this branch of immunotherapy treatments is hugely promising – especially since this experimental CAR T cell therapy produced a remission in a patient with a solid tumor.
paras.zh: 正如研究人员指出的那样，肝癌是全球癌症相关死亡的第三大原因，因此在免疫疗法的这一领域取得进展是非常有希望的——特别是因为这种实验性 CAR T 细胞疗法使实体瘤患者得到了缓解。

paras.en: Related: A Woman With 3 Autoimmune Diseases Entered Remission After an Immune 'Reset'
paras.zh: 相关：一名患有 3 种自身免疫性疾病的女性在免疫“重置”后进入缓解期

paras.en: Of course, it's worth pointing out that this is just a single report of one patient in an early-phase trial, and we'll need to see how other patients respond to the GPC3-CAR treatment before researchers know how effective and safe it is.
paras.zh: 当然，值得指出的是，这只是早期试验中一名患者的单一报告，我们需要看看其他患者对 GPC3-CAR 治疗的反应如何，然后研究人员才能知道它的有效性和安全性。

paras.en: Continued testing is being carried out in the CARE study (at Baylor College of Medicine) and in a similar clinical trial called IMPACT, being run through Seattle Children's Hospital.
paras.zh: 贝勒医学院的 CARE 研究和西雅图儿童医院正在进行的一项名为 IMPACT 的类似临床试验正在继续进行测试。

paras.en: The hope is that, with time, we'll see more positive outcomes like this.
paras.zh: 希望随着时间的推移，我们会看到更多这样的积极成果。

paras.en: For now, we're off to a very promising start.
paras.zh: 目前，我们已经有了一个非常有希望的开始。

paras.en: The findings are reported in The New England Journal of Medicine.
paras.zh: 研究结果发表在《新英格兰医学杂志》上。

articles.title: Scientists Discover Cockroaches Doing Something Surprisingly Useful in The Amazon After Dark
articles.author: Esra Öz

paras.en: At about a quarter to six in the evening, the flowers on a small shrub in the Brazilian Amazon begin to open. Their scent is faint at first. As it grows stronger, nectar starts to trickle down the stalks of the hanging flower clusters.
paras.zh: 大约晚上六点一刻左右，巴西亚马逊地区的一种小灌木上的花朵开始开放。一开始它们的气味很微​​弱。当它变得更强时，花蜜开始从悬挂的花簇的茎上滴下来。

paras.en: Around seven, the first cockroaches arrive.
paras.zh: 七点左右，第一批蟑螂到达。

paras.en: Bats are among the main pollinators of two related species, and this shrub shares some of their features, including flowers that open around dusk and produce plenty of nectar.
paras.zh: 蝙蝠是两个相关物种的主要传粉媒介之一，这种灌木具有一些相似的特征，包括在黄昏时开放并产生大量花蜜的花朵。

paras.en: Yet in a new study published in the Brazilian Journal of Botany, the first to examine how this shrub is pollinated, the researchers recorded no bat visits.
paras.zh: 然而，在《巴西植物学杂志》上发表的一项新研究中，研究人员首次研究了这种灌木如何授粉，但研究人员没有记录到蝙蝠的来访。

paras.en: The team found no nectar in the flowers from 9 am to 5 pm. After dark, cockroaches appeared to be among the shrub's most important pollinators.
paras.zh: 上午9点到下午5点，研究小组在花朵中没有发现花蜜。天黑后，蟑螂似乎是灌木最重要的传粉者之一。

paras.en: Only about 1 percent of cockroach species are household pests, and wild cockroaches are rarely observed visiting flowers.
paras.zh: 只有大约 1% 的蟑螂种类是家庭害虫，而且很少观察到野生蟑螂造访花卉。

paras.en: "It was never imagined that this type of interaction could occur in the Amazon, let alone contribute to reproduction, as the vast majority of attention goes to bees and bats," Tulio Alex Martins-Silva, a botanist at Brazil's National Institute of Amazonian Research, told ScienceAlert.
paras.zh: 巴西国家亚马逊研究所的植物学家图利奥·亚历克斯·马丁斯·席尔瓦（Tulio Alex Martins-Silva）告诉《ScienceAlert》：“从来没有想过这种类型的相互作用会发生在亚马逊，更不用说促进繁殖了，因为绝大多数注意力都集中在蜜蜂和蝙蝠身上。”

paras.en: The team wanted to know which animals might carry pollen between shrubs and how much pollen from another plant mattered for fruit production. The cockroaches offered a clue when they stopped to drink.
paras.zh: 研究小组想知道哪些动物可能在灌木之间携带花粉，以及另一种植物的花粉对水果生产有多少影响。当蟑螂停下来喝水时，它们提供了线索。

paras.en: A cockroach "has to bend its head down to reach the nectar, getting dusted with pollen all over again," Martins-Silva explained.
paras.zh: 马丁斯-席尔瓦解释说，蟑螂“必须低下头才能接触花蜜，再次沾满花粉”。

paras.en: The shrub, Mabea uleana, belongs to the spurge family and grows only in Brazil's Amazonas state, in patches of vegetation on nutrient-poor white sand.
paras.zh: 这种灌木 Mabea uleana 属于大戟科，仅生长在巴西亚马逊州营养贫乏的白沙上的小片植被中。

paras.en: A hanging flower cluster is 4 to 6 centimeters (about 2 inches) long, roughly the length of a thumb. Near the stalk sit one or two female flowers that can develop into fruit. Below them are usually more than 200 tiny male flowers that release pollen.
paras.zh: 悬挂的花簇长 4 至 6 厘米（约 2 英寸），大约有拇指的长度。茎附近有一两朵雌花，可以发育成果实。它们下面通常有 200 多朵释放花粉的微小雄花。

paras.en: A cockroach brushes past the female flowers on its way down to feed. By the time it reaches the nectar, pollen from the male flowers has stuck to its legs and belly. On its way out, it climbs back up the same stalk and touches the female flowers again.
paras.zh: 一只蟑螂在下来觅食的过程中掠过雌花。当它到达花蜜时，雄花的花粉已经粘在它的腿和腹部上。在出去的过程中，它又爬回同一根茎上，再次接触雌花。

paras.en: If the cockroach is already carrying pollen from another shrub when it arrives, it could leave some behind before it even gets a drink.
paras.zh: 如果蟑螂到达时已经携带了其他灌木的花粉，它可能会在喝水之前留下一些花粉。

paras.en: "Euphorbiaceae pollen is very sticky," Martins-Silva said, using the scientific name for the spurge family. That helps explain why the grains cling to the insects as they move through the flowers.
paras.zh: “大戟科花粉非常粘，”马丁斯-席尔瓦说，他用的是大戟科的学名。这有助于解释为什么当昆虫穿过花朵时，谷物会粘附在它们身上。

paras.en: Between June 2024 and January 2025, the team spent 252 hours watching flower clusters on six shrubs north of Manaus, dividing its time evenly between day and night.
paras.zh: 2024 年 6 月至 2025 年 1 月期间，该团队花了 252 个小时观察马瑙斯北部六棵灌木上的花簇，白天和黑夜的时间均等。

paras.en: In a separate experiment, the researchers gave some flowers pollen from their own cluster and others pollen from a different shrub. A third group stayed open to visitors.
paras.zh: 在另一项实验中，研究人员给一些花提供了来自自己簇的花粉，另一些则提供了来自不同灌木的花粉。第三组仍对游客开放。

paras.en: Martins-Silva and botanist Layon Oreste Demarchi, a study co-author, analyzed the data.
paras.zh: 马丁斯-席尔瓦和研究合著者、植物学家莱昂·奥雷斯特·德马奇分析了这些数据。

paras.en: About 93 percent of the flowers given pollen from another shrub formed fruit, compared with 15 percent of those given pollen from their own cluster. About 73 percent of flowers left open to visitors produced fruit. For this shrub, a visitor that brings pollen from another plant could make a big difference.
paras.zh: 接受其他灌木花粉的花朵中，约 93% 会结出果实，而接受自身花簇花粉的花朵中，只有 15% 会结出果实。大约 73% 向游客开放的花朵结出了果实。对于这种灌木来说，来自另一种植物的花粉的访客可能会产生很大的影响。

paras.en: There's a precedent. In an earlier study in French Guiana, researchers estimated that cockroaches pollinated about 41 percent of the structures that could develop into seeds in another tropical shrub.
paras.zh: 有先例。在法属圭亚那的一项早期研究中，研究人员估计蟑螂为另一种热带灌木中约 41% 的结构授粉，这些结构可以发育成种子。

paras.en: The team in Brazil recorded 18 cockroach visits. Martins-Silva suspects they missed some.
paras.zh: 巴西团队记录了 18 次蟑螂来访。马丁斯-席尔瓦怀疑他们错过了一些。

paras.en: "Cockroaches are very sensitive to light, noise, and human presence, so my own presence may have contributed to the low visitation rate," he cautioned.
paras.zh: “蟑螂对光、噪音和人类的存在非常敏感，所以我自己的存在可能导致了蟑螂的低访问率，”他警告说。

paras.en: Small flies and moths also visited after dark. By day, stingless bees called Trigona almeidae were the most frequent visitors. They touched the female flowers as they gathered leftover pollen, and the researchers identified them as likely daytime pollinators.
paras.zh: 天黑后小苍蝇和飞蛾也会来访。白天，最常到访的是被称为 Trigona almeidae 的无刺蜜蜂。他们在收集剩余花粉时触摸了雌花，研究人员确定它们可能是白天传粉者。

paras.en: The study took place at one site, and the fruit experiment didn't measure how much each group contributed.
paras.zh: 这项研究在一个地点进行，水果实验没有测量每组贡献了多少。

paras.en: Other familiar insects, including crickets and grasshoppers, may also move pollen.
paras.zh: 其他常见的昆虫，包括蟋蟀和蚱蜢，也可能传播花粉。

paras.en: A daytime survey of this Amazon shrub would have caught the bees at work. But to see what the cockroaches were doing on the same flowers, the researchers had to stay after dark.
paras.zh: 如果白天对这片亚马逊灌木丛进行调查，就会发现正在工作的蜜蜂。但为了了解蟑螂在同一朵花上做了什么，研究人员必须在天黑后留下来。

paras.en: The research has been published in the Brazilian Journal of Botany.
paras.zh: 该研究已发表在《巴西植物学杂志》上。

articles.title: Even scientists can't agree on what science actually is

paras.en: Even scientists can't agree on what science actually is
paras.zh: 就连科学家也无法就科学到底是什么达成一致

paras.en: - Scientists cannot agree on what science actually is, and a new study finds their views are surprisingly more divided than those of the general public. The findings could help explain public frustration with scientific uncertainty and raise questions about how artificial intelligence might reshape future discoveries.
paras.zh: - 科学家们无法就科学到底是什么达成一致，一项新的研究发现，他们的观点比公众的观点更加分歧。这些发现可能有助于解释公众对科学不确定性的不满，并提出人工智能如何重塑未来发现的问题。

paras.en: Scientists dedicate their careers to uncovering how the world works, yet they have surprisingly different opinions about what science actually means. New research reveals that scientists disagree about the nature and purpose of science even more than the general public does.
paras.zh: 科学家们致力于揭示世界是如何运转的，但他们对科学的真正含义却有着令人惊讶的不同看法。新的研究表明，科学家们对科学的本质和目的的分歧甚至比公众还要多。

paras.en: The study, published in Royal Society Open Science, examined 18 different descriptions of science and found that researchers rarely embraced any of them without reservations. Even when scientists generally supported a particular definition, many questioned some aspect of it.
paras.zh: 这项发表在《皇家学会开放科学》上的研究审查了 18 种不同的科学描述，发现研究人员很少毫无保留地接受其中任何一种。即使科学家普遍支持某个特定定义，许多人仍对其某些方面提出质疑。

paras.en: "What was surprising to me was that there was quite a bit of disagreement between scientists, including scientists who are in the same subfield," says Marina Dubova, who led the research while working as a postdoctoral researcher at the Santa Fe Institute.
paras.zh: “令我惊讶的是，科学家之间存在相当大的分歧，包括同一子领域的科学家，”在圣菲研究所担任博士后研究员期间领导这项研究的玛丽娜·杜博娃 (Marina Dubova) 说。

paras.en: Members of the public, by comparison, expressed more consistent views. They were more likely to regard science as a dependable way to discover objective truths about the world, placing less importance on the uncertainty and creativity involved in scientific research.
paras.zh: 相比之下，公众表达的观点更为一致。他们更有可能将科学视为发现世界客观真理的可靠方式，不太重视科学研究中涉及的不确定性和创造力。

paras.en: These contrasting perspectives may have important consequences. They could affect the questions scientists choose to investigate and influence how people evaluate scientific findings. They may also help explain why the public sometimes becomes frustrated when researchers cannot offer clear answers or change their conclusions in response to new evidence.
paras.zh: 这些截然不同的观点可能会产生重要的后果。它们可能会影响科学家选择调查的问题，并影响人们如何评估科学发现。它们还可能有助于解释为什么当研究人员无法提供明确答案或根据新证据改变结论时，公众有时会感到沮丧。

paras.en: What Scientists and the Public Believe About Science
paras.zh: 科学家和公众对科学的看法

paras.en: Dubova, now an assistant professor of psychology at the University of California, Berkeley, worked with Princeton University researcher Qiawen E. Liu to investigate how people understand science.
paras.zh: 杜波娃现为加州大学伯克利分校心理学助理教授，她与普林斯顿大学研究员刘恰文 (Qiawen E. Liu) 合作研究人们如何理解科学。

paras.en: The researchers surveyed 91 scientists and 99 members of the public. Participants were asked to assess 18 descriptions of science drawn from historical perspectives, including comparisons of scientific research to detective work, a pursuit of truth, and a mirror that reflects reality.
paras.zh: 研究人员对 91 名科学家和 99 名公众进行了调查。参与者被要求评估 18 种从历史角度对科学的描述，包括科学研究与侦探工作的比较、对真理的追求以及反映现实的镜子。

paras.en: Both groups generally agreed that curiosity, exploration, and the desire to solve mysteries are central to science. Beyond those shared ideas, however, the scientists expressed strikingly different perspectives.
paras.zh: 两个群体普遍认为好奇心、探索和解开谜团的渴望是科学的核心。然而，除了这些共同的想法之外，科学家们还表达了截然不同的观点。

paras.en: Some researchers viewed science primarily as a means of discovering objective truths. Others placed greater importance on imagination, personal judgment, and the creative decisions involved in research. Scientists also differed over whether scientific progress depends mainly on following established procedures or adapting and improvising as new challenges arise.
paras.zh: 一些研究人员将科学主要视为发现客观真理的一种手段。其他人则更加重视想象力、个人判断以及研究中涉及的创造性决策。对于科学进步主要取决于遵循既定程序还是在新挑战出现时进行调整和即兴发挥，科学家们也存在分歧。

paras.en: Dubova believes these disagreements may reflect the individual experiences that shape how researchers approach their work. Just as chefs can have very different philosophies about preparing food, scientists can develop distinct ideas about the best ways to investigate the world.
paras.zh: 杜博娃认为，这些分歧可能反映了影响研究人员工作方式的个人经历。正如厨师在准备食物时可能有不同的理念一样，科学家也可以就探索世界的最佳方式提出不同的想法。

paras.en: Another intriguing finding involved differences among scientific disciplines. The general public's understanding of science more closely resembled the views expressed by physicists and biologists than those of psychologists and other social scientists.
paras.zh: 另一个有趣的发现涉及科学学科之间的差异。公众对科学的理解更接近于物理学家和生物学家所表达的观点，而不是心理学家和其他社会科学家的观点。

paras.en: One possible reason is that physics and biology receive greater attention in science education, potentially shaping how people imagine scientific research. Dubova emphasizes, however, that this explanation remains tentative and will require additional investigation.
paras.zh: 一个可能的原因是物理和生物学在科学教育中受到更多关注，可能会影响人们对科学研究的想象。然而，杜博娃强调，这种解释仍然是暂时的，需要进一步调查。

paras.en: The differences between scientists and the public could also help explain misunderstandings about scientific uncertainty. People who expect science to produce firm, objective answers may have difficulty understanding why findings sometimes conflict or why scientific conclusions must be updated when new evidence becomes available.
paras.zh: 科学家和公众之间的差异也可能有助于解释对科学不确定性的误解。那些期望科学能够给出坚定、客观答案的人们可能很难理解为什么研究结果有时会发生冲突，或者为什么当新证据出现时必须更新科学结论。

paras.en: What the Findings Could Mean for AI and Scientific Discovery
paras.zh: 这些发现对人工智能和科学发现意味着什么

paras.en: The research also points to a potential challenge as artificial intelligence becomes increasingly involved in scientific discovery.
paras.zh: 该研究还指出了随着人工智能越来越多地参与科学发现而面临的潜在挑战。

paras.en: With researchers developing AI systems that can carry out scientific investigations, Dubova is concerned that automation could favor a limited conception of how science should work. If those systems are built around one particular approach to research, other valuable methods of discovery could receive less attention.
paras.zh: 随着研究人员开发可以进行科学研究的人工智能系统，杜博娃担心自动化可能会支持科学应该如何运作的有限概念。如果这些系统是围绕一种特定的研究方法构建的，那么其他有价值的发现方法可能会受到较少的关注。

paras.en: The study received support from the Santa Fe Institute's Lou Schuyler Seed Grant Fund, which was created in 2022 to encourage exploratory projects by early career scientists. Dubova used the funding to pay participants for taking part in the research.
paras.zh: 该研究得到了圣达菲研究所 Lou Schuyler 种子资助基金的支持，该基金于 2022 年创建，旨在鼓励早期职业科学家的探索性项目。杜博娃用这笔资金支付参与者参与研究的费用。

paras.en: For Dubova, the findings represent an initial effort to understand how scientists' underlying beliefs about their profession might influence the research they conduct and the discoveries they make.
paras.zh: 对于杜博娃来说，这些发现代表了了解科学家对其职业的基本信念如何影响他们进行的研究和发现的初步努力。

paras.en: "Don't take the common understanding of science for granted," she says. "Always ask. Always be curious about what someone has in mind."
paras.zh: “不要把对科学的普遍理解视为理所当然，”她说。 “永远要问。永远对某人的想法感到好奇。”

paras.en: Materials provided by Santa Fe Institute. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
paras.zh: 材料由圣达菲研究所提供。注意：内容可能会根据样式和长度进行编辑。

paras.en: - Marina Dubova, Qiawen E. Liu. Everyone knows what science isâ¦until you ask. Royal Society Open Science, 2026; 13 (11) DOI: 10.1098/rsos.260933
paras.zh: - 玛丽娜·杜博娃 (Marina Dubova)，刘恰文 (Qiawen E. Liu)。每个人都知道科学是什么……直到你问。英国皇家学会开放科学，2026； 13（11）DOI：10.1098/rsos.260933

articles.title: A 50-year-old theory about evolution may have been wrong all along

paras.en: A 50-year-old theory about evolution may have been wrong all along
paras.zh: 已有 50 年历史的进化论可能一直都是错误的

paras.en: - A decades-old theory suggesting that evolution protects its most important genes from mutations has been dealt a major blow. An extensive new analysis of mutations in bacteria and yeast found no evidence that essential genes mutate less frequently than other genes. Researchers say earlier studies may have been misled by harmful mutations that disappeared through natural selection before scientists could detect them.
paras.zh: - 几十年前的理论认为进化可以保护其最重要的基因免受突变，但这一理论受到了重大打击。对细菌和酵母突变的广泛新分析发现，没有证据表明必需基因的突变频率低于其他基因。研究人员表示，早期的研究可能被有害突变所误导，这些突变在科学家发现之前就通过自然选择消失了。

paras.en: For more than 50 years, scientists have debated a provocative idea about evolution: Could organisms protect their most important genes by making them less likely to mutate? First proposed in 1972, the hypothesis challenges the traditional understanding of how genetic changes arise. Now, new research from the University of Bath suggests that the evidence supporting this idea has been misleading.
paras.zh: 50多年来，科学家们一直在争论关于进化的一个具有争议性的观点：生物体能否通过降低基因突变的可能性来保护它们最重要的基因？该假说于 1972 年首次提出，挑战了对遗传变化如何发生的传统理解。现在，巴斯大学的新研究表明，支持这一观点的证据具有误导性。

paras.en: In a study published in PLOS Biology, Dr. Sofia Radrizzani and Professor Laurence D Hurst of the University of Bath's Centre for Evolution examined the largest collection of spontaneous genetic mutations assembled to date. Their analysis focused on two microorganisms: the bacterium Escherichia coli (E. coli) and the single-celled fungus baker's yeast (Saccharomyces cerevisiae).
paras.zh: 在《PLOS Biology》上发表的一项研究中，巴斯大学进化中心的 Sofia Radrizzani 博士和 Laurence D Hurst 教授检查了迄今为止最大的自发基因突变集合。他们的分析集中在两种微生物：大肠杆菌（E. coli）和单细胞真菌面包酵母（酿酒酵母）。

paras.en: The findings challenge the claim that natural selection can reduce mutation rates in genes essential for survival. Although this theory has repeatedly attracted scientific attention since its introduction, including a renewed debate in 2023, the researchers say their results undermine its central premise.
paras.zh: 这些发现对自然选择可以降低生存必需基因突变率的说法提出了挑战。尽管这一理论自提出以来多次引起科学界的关注，包括 2023 年再次引发的争论，但研究人员表示，他们的结果破坏了其核心前提。

paras.en: "The claim that mutation is slower for important genes is a triumph of hype over substance," said Dr. Radrizzani, who co-wrote the new paper as part of her PhD. "It's a really old suggestion and is reinvented in various forms routinely."
paras.zh: “重要基因的突变速度较慢的说法是炒作战胜了实质内容，”拉德里扎尼博士说，她是这篇新论文的合著者，作为她博士论文的一部分。 “这是一个非常古老的建议，并且经常以各种形式重新发明。”

paras.en: How Mutations and Natural Selection Drive Evolution
paras.zh: 突变和自然选择如何推动进化

paras.en: The conventional explanation of evolution involves two main processes. Genetic mutations first introduce variation among organisms. Natural selection then influences which of those variations become more common, favoring traits that improve survival and reproduction. This process can be compared to a sieve that separates different kinds of material, allowing some genetic changes to persist while others disappear.
paras.zh: 进化论的传统解释涉及两个主要过程。基因突变首先引入生物体之间的变异。然后，自然选择会影响哪些变异变得更加普遍，从而有利于改善生存和繁殖的特征。这个过程就像一个筛子，可以分离不同种类的物质，让一些基因变化持续存在，而另一些则消失。

paras.en: A familiar example comes from Darwin's finches, which Charles Darwin first encountered on the Galápagos Islands in 1835. These birds have different beak shapes that help them feed on different foods. Random mutations contribute to variations in beak size and shape, and when certain food sources become more plentiful, birds with better-suited beaks are more likely to survive and reproduce. Over many generations, these advantageous traits can spread through the population.
paras.zh: 一个熟悉的例子是达尔文雀，查尔斯·达尔文于 1835 年在加拉帕戈斯群岛首次遇到这种雀。这些鸟具有不同的喙形状，有助于它们捕食不同的食物。随机突变会导致喙的大小和形状发生变化，当某些食物来源变得更加丰富时，具有更适合喙的鸟类更有可能生存和繁殖。经过许多代，这些有利的特征可以在人群中传播。

paras.en: However, an alternative hypothesis suggests that mutations may not occur as randomly as the conventional model assumes. According to this idea, organisms have evolved ways to reduce mutations in their most critical genes (such as those involved in replicating DNA or maintaining basic cellular machinery). Meanwhile, genes in which changes might provide useful adaptations (such as those in which mutations give bacteria resistance to antibiotics, or change beak dimensions) could experience higher mutation rates.
paras.zh: 然而，另一种假设表明，突变可能不会像传统模型假设的那样随机发生。根据这个想法，生物体已经进化出减少其最关键基因（例如涉及复制 DNA 或维持基本细胞机制的基因）突变的方法。与此同时，那些变化可能提供有用适应的基因（例如那些突变使细菌对抗生素产生抗性，或改变喙尺寸的基因）可能会经历更高的突变率。

paras.en: At first glance, protecting essential genes seems like an obvious evolutionary advantage. Mutations affecting these genes can disrupt vital biological processes, cause genetic diseases, or even kill an organism. If such changes are so dangerous, why wouldn't natural selection favor mechanisms that prevent them?
paras.zh: 乍一看，保护必需基因似乎是一个明显的进化优势。影响这些基因的突变可能会破坏重要的生物过程，引起遗传疾病，甚至杀死有机体。如果这种变化如此危险，为什么自然选择不支持阻止它们的机制呢？

paras.en: The problem, researchers explain, is that mutations in individual genes are already relatively rare. Reducing those rates even further would provide only a tiny additional benefit, making it difficult for natural selection to favor such a protective system.
paras.zh: 研究人员解释说，问题在于单个基因的突变已经相对罕见。进一步降低这些比率只会带来微小的额外好处，使得自然选择很难支持这样的保护系统。

paras.en: The Mystery of Disappearing Genetic Mutations
paras.zh: 消失的基因突变之谜

paras.en: Another problem lies in how scientists have measured mutations in earlier research. Important genes may appear to mutate less frequently not because they are better protected, but because harmful mutations in those genes are quickly eliminated from populations.
paras.zh: 另一个问题在于科学家如何在早期研究中测量突变。重要基因的突变频率可能较低，并不是因为它们受到更好的保护，而是因为这些基因中的有害突变很快就会从种群中消除。

paras.en: Professor Hurst said: "We'd expect natural selection to rapidly remove mutations when they occur in more important genes, because these mutations are more likely to be harmful to the organism. This can create the illusion that important genes have fewer mutations when, in reality, some mutations have simply disappeared before we have a chance to analyze them - what you can think of as 'ghost mutations'."
paras.zh: 赫斯特教授说：“我们期望自然选择能够在更重要的基因中发生突变时迅速消除它们，因为这些突变更有可能对生物体有害。这可能会造成一种错觉，即重要基因的突变较少，而实际上，一些突变在我们有机会分析它们之前就已经消失了——你可以将其视为‘幽灵突变’。”

paras.en: This distinction is crucial. When scientists examine the genetic changes remaining in a population, they may miss mutations that occurred but were subsequently removed by natural selection. As a result, the apparent stability of essential genes could reflect the disappearance of damaging mutations rather than a lower likelihood of those mutations occurring in the first place.
paras.zh: 这种区别至关重要。当科学家检查种群中剩余的遗传变化时，他们可能会错过发生但随后被自然选择消除的突变。因此，必需基因的表观稳定性可能反映了破坏性突变的消失，而不是这些突变首先发生的可能性较低。

paras.en: A Major Test of the 50-Year-Old Evolutionary Theory
paras.zh: 对50年进化论的重大考验

paras.en: To investigate the question more directly, the University of Bath team analyzed data from experiments designed to record mutations while minimizing the influence of natural selection. These experiments, known as mutation accumulation studies, allowed researchers to examine genetic changes in E. coli and baker's yeast without the usual strong filtering effects of selection.
paras.zh: 为了更直接地研究这个问题，巴斯大学团队分析了旨在记录突变的实验数据，同时最大限度地减少自然选择的影响。这些实验被称为突变积累研究，使研究人员能够检查大肠杆菌和面包酵母的遗传变化，而无需通常的强烈选择过滤效应。

paras.en: The scientists also performed three independent tests to determine whether natural selection might still have significantly distorted the data. None revealed evidence of substantial bias.
paras.zh: 科学家们还进行了三项独立测试，以确定自然选择是否仍然会严重扭曲数据。没有人发现存在重大偏见的证据。

paras.en: Dr. Radrizzani said: "This looks like the largest and cleanest sample of mutations assembled to date."
paras.zh: 拉德里扎尼博士说：“这看起来是迄今为止组装的最大、最干净的突变样本。”

paras.en: With this extensive dataset, the researchers investigated whether genes that are more important for survival actually experience fewer mutations.
paras.zh: 通过这个广泛的数据集，研究人员调查了对生存更重要的基因是否实际上经历了更少的突变。

paras.en: They assessed gene importance using experiments in which individual genes were removed from organisms. Some genes are indispensable, meaning that cells die without them. Others can be deleted with little or no noticeable effect.
paras.zh: 他们通过从生物体中去除单个基因的实验来评估基因的重要性。有些基因是不可或缺的，这意味着细胞没有它们就会死亡。其他的可以删除，影响很小或没有明显影响。

paras.en: If the protective mutation hypothesis were correct, the most essential genes should have shown consistently lower mutation rates. Instead, the researchers found no such relationship in either microorganism.
paras.zh: 如果保护性突变假说是正确的，那么最重要的基因应该表现出持续较低的突变率。相反，研究人员在这两种微生物中都没有发现这种关系。

paras.en: Professor Hurst said: "Analyze the data any which way and we found nothing. In neither species did these key genes have a lower mutation rate."
paras.zh: 赫斯特教授说：“无论以哪种方式分析数据，我们都没有发现任何结果。在这两个物种中，这些关键基因的突变率都不低。”

paras.en: What Really Determines How Often Genes Mutate?
paras.zh: 到底是什么决定了基因突变的频率？

paras.en: The team also examined whether other measures of gene importance could explain differences in mutation rates. These included the amount of protein produced by each gene and how strongly natural selection had shaped genes over thousands of years.
paras.zh: 研究小组还研究了基因重要性的其他衡量标准是否可以解释突变率的差异。其中包括每个基因产生的蛋白质数量，以及数千年来自然选择对基因的塑造程度。

paras.en: Once again, the results failed to support the idea that more important genes receive special protection.
paras.zh: 结果再次未能支持更重要的基因受到特殊保护的观点。

paras.en: Dr. Radrizzani said: "We found that genes producing more abundant proteins don't have lower mutation rates. Nor does the way genes evolve over thousands of years predict how frequently they mutate."
paras.zh: Radrizzani 博士说：“我们发现产生更丰富蛋白质的基因并不具有较低的突变率。基因数千年的进化方式也不能预测它们突变的频率。”

paras.en: That does not mean every gene has exactly the same chance of mutating. The researchers identified features of genome structure and DNA replication that influence mutation frequency. For example, genes copied later during DNA replication tend to accumulate mutations more frequently than those copied earlier.
paras.zh: 这并不意味着每个基因都有完全相同的突变机会。研究人员确定了影响突变频率的基因组结构和 DNA 复制特征。例如，在 DNA 复制过程中，较晚复制的基因往往比较早复制的基因更频繁地积累突变。

paras.en: These findings indicate that mutation rates can vary across the genome, but the differences do not appear to reflect a system that specifically shields essential genes from genetic changes.
paras.zh: 这些发现表明，基因组中的突变率可能有所不同，但这些差异似乎并不反映有一个专门保护必需基因免受遗传变化影响的系统。

paras.en: Professor Hurst said: "While we see known causes of variation in mutation rates, we found no evidence for the effects that have been proposed as a challenge to the conventional model. None predicted which genes would have high or low mutation rates, and there are certainly no grounds for a shift in paradigm."
paras.zh: 赫斯特教授说：“虽然我们看到了突变率变异的已知原因，但我们没有发现任何证据表明这些影响被认为是对传统模型的挑战。没有人预测哪些基因会具有高或低的突变率，而且当然没有理由改变范式。”

paras.en: The research therefore provides new support for the conventional distinction between mutation and natural selection. Although mutations do not occur at identical rates everywhere in the genome, the evidence from bacteria and yeast offers no indication that evolution systematically protects its most important genes by reducing how often they mutate.
paras.zh: 因此，这项研究为突变和自然选择之间的传统区别提供了新的支持。尽管基因组中各处的突变发生率并不相同，但来自细菌和酵母的证据并没有表明进化通过减少突变频率来系统地保护其最重要的基因。

paras.en: Materials provided by University of Bath. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
paras.zh: 材料由巴斯大学提供。注意：内容可能会根据样式和长度进行编辑。

paras.en: - Sofia Radrizzani, Laurence D. Hurst. The importance of genes does not predict their mutation rate. PLOS Biology, 2026; 24 (11): e3004089 DOI: 10.1371/journal.pbio.3004089
paras.zh: - 索菲亚·拉德里扎尼，劳伦斯·D·赫斯特。基因的重要性并不能预测其突变率。 PLOS 生物学，2026； 24 (11): e3004089 DOI: 10.1371/journal.pbio.3004089

articles.title: Who was buried in Westminster Abbey's Roman coffin? A 150-year mystery may be solved

paras.en: Who was buried in Westminster Abbey's Roman coffin? A 150-year mystery may be solved
paras.zh: 谁被埋在威斯敏斯特教堂的罗马棺材里？ 150年之谜有望解开

paras.en: - A mysterious skeleton discovered in a Roman sarcophagus at Westminster Abbey may finally be identified after more than 150 years. New dating evidence suggests the remains belonged to a high-ranking medieval abbot who was buried inside a centuries-old recycled Roman coffin.
paras.zh: - 在威斯敏斯特教堂的罗马石棺中发现的神秘骨架可能在 150 多年后终于被辨认出来。新的年代测定证据表明，这些遗骸属于一位中世纪高级修道院院长，他被埋在一个有数百年历史的回收罗马棺材内。

paras.en: A mystery surrounding a skeleton discovered inside an ancient Roman coffin at Westminster Abbey may finally be approaching a solution, more than 150 years after the remains first attracted attention.
paras.zh: 在威斯敏斯特教堂的古罗马棺材内发现的一具骸骨的谜团可能终于要解开，距该遗骸首次引起关注已经过去了 150 多年。

paras.en: The limestone sarcophagus, formally excavated in 1869, carries an inscription naming Valerius Amandinus, a wealthy Briton who lived in London sometime between 300 and 400 AD. However, a large Latin cross carved into its lid dates to approximately the 10th or 11th century, suggesting that the person buried inside lived hundreds of years after the coffin was originally made.
paras.zh: 石灰石石棺于 1869 年正式出土，刻有铭文，名字为瓦莱里乌斯·阿曼迪努斯 (Valerius Amandinus)，他是一位富有的英国人，公元 300 年至 400 年期间居住在伦敦。然而，棺盖上刻有一个大型拉丁十字，其历史可追溯到大约 10 世纪或 11 世纪，这表明埋在里面的人在棺材最初制作后已经生活了数百年。

paras.en: Now, fresh archaeological research points to a surprising explanation. The remains likely belong to a prominent medieval monk, and researchers have narrowed the possible identities to two men who once led Westminster Abbey.
paras.zh: 现在，新的考古研究给出了一个令人惊讶的解释。这些遗骸可能属于一位著名的中世纪僧侣，研究人员已将可能的身份缩小到曾经领导威斯敏斯特教堂的两名男子。

paras.en: Two Medieval Abbots Emerge as Leading Candidates
paras.zh: 两位中世纪修道院院长成为主要候选人

paras.en: The new findings, published in the peer-reviewed Journal of the British Archaeological Association, come from Professor Warwick Rodwell, Consultant Archaeologist at Westminster Abbey.
paras.zh: 这项新发现发表在经过同行评审的《英国考古协会杂志》上，来自威斯敏斯特教堂考古顾问沃里克·罗德威尔教授。

paras.en: Rodwell identifies Aelfwig, an abbot who died around 1020, as the strongest candidate. At the time, Westminster Abbey was a Benedictine monastery, and Aelfwig had served there as a monk before becoming its abbot.
paras.zh: 罗德威尔认为 1020 年左右去世的修道院院长艾尔夫维格是最有力的候选人。当时，威斯敏斯特教堂是一座本笃会修道院，艾尔夫维格在成为修道院院长之前曾在那里担任修道士。

paras.en: Another possibility is Wulnoth, who succeeded Aelfwig and died in 1049. Both men are believed to have been buried at the Abbey, making either a plausible match for the skeleton.
paras.zh: 另一种可能性是乌尔诺斯 (Wulnoth)，他继承了艾尔夫维格 (Aelfwig) 的王位，于 1049 年去世。 据信，这两个人都被埋葬在修道院内，因此两人的骸骨似乎都相符。

paras.en: "We have two viable contenders for the occupant of the sarcophagus," says Professor Rodwell, Consultant Archaeologist at Westminster Abbey.
paras.zh: 威斯敏斯特教堂考古顾问顾问罗德威尔教授说：“对于石棺的主人，我们有两个可行的竞争者。”

paras.en: "We do not know the date of birth of either. But either would fit equally well if we assume the Abbot was in his early twenties when the appointment was made and close to fifty when he died.
paras.zh: “我们不知道他们的出生日期。但如果我们假设方丈在任命时二十岁出头，去世时已接近五十岁，那么两者都同样合适。

paras.en: "The fact Aelfwig was already a monk of Westminster might favor him."
paras.zh: “艾尔夫维格已经是威斯敏斯特的僧侣，这一事实可能对他有利。”

paras.en: The elaborate burial provides another reason to suspect that the deceased held an important position. Rodwell suggests that the individual was 'honored' with a 'fine sarcophagus', an unusual distinction that would be consistent with the status of an abbot.
paras.zh: 精心设计的墓葬提供了另一个怀疑死者担任重要职务的理由。罗德威尔认为，这个人被“授予”了“精致的石棺”，这是一种不寻常的区别，与修道院院长的地位相符。

paras.en: Rather than commissioning an entirely new stone coffin, those responsible for the burial apparently reused an existing Roman sarcophagus. The man's wooden coffin was placed inside it, and the stone lid was modified with a prominent Latin cross. This may represent an early example of recycling a valuable object for an entirely different purpose.
paras.zh: 负责埋葬的人显然没有委托建造全新的石棺，而是重复使用了现有的罗马石棺。里面放着这名男子的木棺，石盖上刻有醒目的拉丁十字。这可能代表了为完全不同的目的回收有价值的物品的早期例子。

paras.en: New Excavations Reveal the Skeleton's Age
paras.zh: 新的发掘揭示了骨骼的年龄

paras.en: The Roman sarcophagus and its mysterious occupant have fascinated researchers for generations. Rodwell's latest conclusions draw on several investigations conducted with specialists over the years, including work associated with Channel 4's Time Team.
paras.zh: 罗马石棺及其神秘的主人让几代研究人员着迷。罗德威尔的最新结论基于多年来与专家进行的多项调查，其中包括与第四频道时间团队相关的工作。

paras.en: In 2009, the television program examined the archaeology and architecture of King Henry III's original sacristy, located along the north side of Westminster Abbey.
paras.zh: 2009 年，该电视节目考察了亨利三世国王最初的圣器收藏室（位于威斯敏斯特教堂北侧）的考古学和建筑。

paras.en: The same area was the scene of an earlier accidental discovery in 1820, when workers encountered the Roman coffin and broke its lid into six pieces. The damage was repaired around the time the sarcophagus was formally 'discovered' in 1869.
paras.zh: 1820 年，同一地区曾有过一次意外发现，当时工人们遇到了罗马棺材，并将其盖子打碎成六块。 1869 年石棺被正式“发现”时，损坏的地方得到了修复。

paras.en: More recently, Pre-Construct Archaeology, one of the UK's largest commercial archaeological and heritage organizations, carried out another excavation of the sacristy. Completed in 2025, the project was undertaken to support construction of the King Charles III Sacristy, a new facility at Westminster Abbey scheduled to open the following year.
paras.zh: 最近，英国最大的商业考古和遗产组织之一预建考古学对圣器收藏室进行了另一次挖掘。该项目于 2025 年竣工，旨在支持查理三世国王圣器收藏室的建设，这是威斯敏斯特教堂的一个新设施，计划于次年开放。

paras.en: As part of this investigation, human bone specialist James Young Langthorne of Pre-Construct Archaeology (PCA) conducted a fresh examination of the skeleton.
paras.zh: 作为此次调查的一部分，预建造考古学 (PCA) 的人体骨骼专家 James Young Langthorne 对骨骼进行了重新检查。

paras.en: His analysis indicated that the deceased was a man between 35 and 49 years old who stood approximately 5 feet 9 inches tall. These findings differ considerably from an assessment made in the 1800s, which described the remains as those of a 'robust young man' no older than 30 and approximately 5 feet 7 inches tall.
paras.zh: 他的分析显示，死者是一名35岁至49岁的男性，身高约5英尺9英寸。这些发现与 1800 年代的评估有很大不同，后者将遗骸描述为一名“强壮的年轻人”，年龄不超过 30 岁，身高约 5 英尺 7 英寸。

paras.en: Carbon Dating Confirms a 1,000-Year-Old Burial
paras.zh: 碳测年证实一处墓葬已有 1000 年历史

paras.en: One of the most important clues came from scientific dating of the remains. A bone sample was submitted to the Scottish Universities Environmental Research Centre for radiocarbon analysis, which produced a date range of 987 to 1052 AD.
paras.zh: 最重要的线索之一来自对遗骸的科学年代测定。一份骨头样本被提交给苏格兰大学环境研究中心进行放射性碳分析，得出的日期范围为公元 987 年至 1052 年。

paras.en: This places the burial firmly within the late Saxon period, centuries after the Roman sarcophagus was originally created. The dates also align with the deaths of both Aelfwig and Wulnoth, strengthening the case that the skeleton belonged to one of these medieval abbots.
paras.zh: 这表明该墓葬属于撒克逊晚期，即罗马石棺最初制作几个世纪之后。这些日期也与艾尔夫维格和乌尔诺斯的死亡时间一致，进一步证明了这具骨架属于这些中世纪修道院院长之一。

paras.en: "This confirms that the reuse of the sarcophagus, and the associated remodeling of its cover, occurred in the late Saxon period."
paras.zh: “这证实了石棺的再利用以及对其盖子的相关改造发生在撒克逊时期晚期。”

paras.en: The results provide scientific support for the theory that an ancient Roman burial container was repurposed to honor an important religious figure nearly 1,000 years ago.
paras.zh: 研究结果为这样的理论提供了科学支持：古罗马墓葬容器被重新利用以纪念近 1000 年前的一位重要宗教人物。

paras.en: A Skeleton Thought Lost Was Hiding in Plain Sight
paras.zh: 遗失的骷髅思想隐藏在众目睽睽之下

paras.en: The investigation also brought renewed attention to an unexpected discovery made in 2016. For years, researchers had believed that the skeleton was missing, leaving an important part of the burial's history unresolved.
paras.zh: 这项调查还让人们重新关注 2016 年的一个意外发现。多年来，研究人员一直认为这具骨架失踪了，导致该墓葬历史的一个重要部分仍未解开。

paras.en: That assumption proved mistaken when the sarcophagus was transported to a conservation studio. PCA researchers removed its lid and were surprised to find an almost complete human skeleton still inside.
paras.zh: 当石棺被运到保护工作室时，这一假设被证明是错误的。 PCA 研究人员打开盖子，惊讶地发现里面仍然有几乎完整的人体骨骼。

paras.en: The examination produced another clue that Rodwell describes as a 'remarkable new discovery'. Inside the stone coffin, researchers identified the rectangular outline of a structure that had disappeared long ago. Its shape was preserved by a white residue left behind by lime, a material historically used in burials.
paras.zh: 检查产生了另一条线索，罗德威尔将其描述为“非凡的新发现”。在石棺内，研究人员发现了一个早已消失的结构的矩形轮廓。石灰留下的白色残留物保留了它的形状，石灰是历史上用于墓葬的材料。

paras.en: Rodwell believes the outline marks the position of the original wooden coffin that held the deceased before it was placed inside the Roman sarcophagus.
paras.zh: 罗德威尔认为，这个轮廓标志着死者最初的木棺在被放入罗马石棺之前的位置。

paras.en: "Although no physical traces of that feature remained, it can only have been a timber coffin, which has completely decayed over the course of the seven centuries that the sarcophagus was buried in the sacristy courtyard," writes Professor Rodwell.
paras.zh: 罗德威尔教授写道：“虽然没有留下任何物理痕迹，但它只能是一个木制棺材，在石棺被埋在圣​​器收藏室庭院的七个世纪的过程中，它已经完全腐烂了。”

paras.en: Together, the rediscovered skeleton, evidence of a wooden coffin, and new scientific dating have transformed researchers' understanding of this unusual burial. Although the man's identity has not been established beyond doubt, the findings suggest that a medieval abbot may have been laid to rest in a Roman coffin already centuries old.
paras.zh: 重新发现的骨骼、木棺的证据和新的科学年代测定一起改变了研究人员对这个不寻常墓葬的理解。尽管该男子的身份尚未确定，但调查结果表明，一位中世纪修道院院长可能被安葬在已有数百年历史的罗马棺材中。

paras.en: Visitors can see the sarcophagus today in the Queen's Diamond Jubilee Galleries at Westminster Abbey.
paras.zh: 今天，游客可以在威斯敏斯特教堂的女王登基五十周年纪念画廊中看到石棺。

paras.en: Materials provided by Taylor & Francis Group. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
paras.zh: 材料由 Taylor & Francis Group 提供。注意：内容可能会根据样式和长度进行编辑。

paras.en: - Warwick Rodwell. Westminster Abbeyâs Roman Sarcophagus and its Afterlife. Journal of the British Archaeological Association, 2026; 179 (1): 1 DOI: 10.1080/00681288.2026.2675788
paras.zh: ——沃里克·罗德威尔。威斯敏斯特教堂的罗马石棺及其来世。英国考古协会杂志，2026； 179 (1): 1 DOI: 10.1080/00681288.2026.2675788

articles.title: Could an ancient solar eclipse rewrite Egyptian history?
articles.author: Jamie Carter

paras.en: The solar system is a clock that can be run in both directions. On Aug. 2, 2027, that clock will bring the moon's dark central shadow — a path of totality — back to Egypt.
